units.tr: An ox goring an ox, if it causes a woman's foetus to be expelled. If a man does so, goring a neighbour. How payment for the foetus is made, and how the valuation is done. Regarding a freed female slave and a foreigner, harshness. Note. A special mode of speaking in the Mishnah. Explained from Exod. 21. 22-23. A woman with a foetus, and where she has brought forth the foetus, is compared. That a woman after childbirth is considered the more valuable. What that foreigner and that slave-woman are. The Mishnah contradicts Scripture. A foreigner of another religion is not considered an heir to Jews. A wife is not heir of her husband. Many debts owed on account of an aborted foetus, confirmed from Roman law.

units.la: De puteo effosso varii casus expenduntur. Inde datum damnum. Similia sub puteo comprehendi. Debita putei profunditas. Ann.¹ רמוּח. Os putei considerandum, ubi fit.² Ex. 21.33. restringitur.
units.tr: Various cases concerning a well that has been dug are weighed. Thence the damage given. Similar things are comprehended under "well." The due depth of a well. Note. רמוּח [ramuach]. The mouth of the well is to be considered, where it is made. Exod. 21. 33. is restricted.

units.la: Locus privatus ἀχυρελογία quò transferatur. 1 Explicantur, שיח, מערה, חריין, כעיין.4 Quæ puteo similia sunt, æque profunda sunt.5 De damno etiam tenetur, qui minori profunditate, quam puteus sit, ledit. Mifna respondet l. 28. ff. Ad l. Aquil.
units.tr: A private place: ἀχυρελογία [achyrelogia], to what it is transferred. 1 Explained: [שיח], [מערה], [חריין], [כעיין].4 Those things which are similar to a well are equally deep.5 He who injures with a lesser depth than that of a well is also liable for damage. The Mishnah answers as in the Digest, l. 28, Ad legem Aquiliam.

units.la: Putei aperti nomine quis teneatur. Tegere uti oportet, quanti momenti sit. Modus cadendi, jus mutat. De instrumentis bovis qui incidit. item bove surdo, &c. Filius aut servus si incidant in puteum. Ann.1 Quà conditione posterior, putei nomine teneatur.2 Supinum cadere varios modos admittit.3 De iis quæ in hac causa lacerari & frangi dicuntur.4 Insulsè restringitur Ex. 21. 33. seq.5 Alia ejusdem legis prava restrictio.6 Mifna verba male accipiunt Iudai. Convenienter Mifna, leg. Romana, ledendi occasionem interdicunt.
units.tr: Who is liable on account of an open well. How important it is to cover it. The mode of falling changes the law. Concerning the implements of an ox that falls in, likewise an ox that is deaf, etc. If a son or a slave falls into the well. Note. 1 On what condition the latter is liable on account of a well.2 Falling on the back admits various modes.3 Concerning those things which are said to be torn and broken in this case.4 Foolishly restricted, Exod. 21. 33. following.5 Another perverse restriction of the same law.6 The Jews take the words of the Mishnah wrongly. In agreement with the Mishnah, Roman law forbids the occasion of harming.

units.la: Cadere in puteum aliis pecoribus applicatur. In multis præterea cum fera, tum aves bobus aquantur. Phrasis Exod. 21. 33. ratio. Ann.1 Ex. 19. 13. evolvitur.2 Ex. 22. 9. extenditur.3 Idem in Ex. 23. 5. sit.4 In Deut. 25. 4. similiter. Phrasis Talmudica difficillima & argumentandi modus exponitur.5 De loco Lev. 19. 19. & Deut. 22. c. 10. com.6 Deut. 5. 14. extenditur, si seq. conferantur.7 Ebr. & Roman. formula convenientes. De extendendo genere masculino. In jure dicundo leges ad casus similes extendi, ex ff. probatur. Privilegia tamen non extendi ad alias personas.
units.tr: To fall into a well is applied to other livestock. Moreover, in many cases both wild beasts and birds are equated with oxen. The phrase of Exod. 21. 33., and its reason. Note. 1 Exod. 19. 13. is unfolded.2 Exod. 22. 9. is extended.3 The same is in Exod. 23. 5.4 Likewise in Deut. 25. 4. The very difficult Talmudic phrase and the mode of argument are explained.5 On the passage Lev. 19. 19. and Deut. 22. 10. compared.6 Deut. 5. 14. is extended, if the following passages are compared.7 Hebrew and Roman formulas agree. On extending the masculine gender. In pronouncing law, laws are extended to similar cases, as proved from the Digest. Privileges, however, are not extended to other persons.

units.la: Pecus conclusa, uti oportet; vel contra. De pecude egressa, effracto pariete. Latro si educat. Ann.1 Quid sit concludere uti oportet.2 De pecude parietem dejiciente.3 Quo nomine hic teneantur latrones.4 Quid sit, educere pecudem. Occasio damni, ex utroque jure ad compensationem obligat.
units.tr: Livestock shut in, as it ought to be, or the reverse. Of an animal that goes out after the wall is breached. If a thief leads it out. Annotation. 1 What it means to shut in "as it ought to be." 2 Of an animal that knocks down a wall. 3 On what ground thieves are liable here. 4 What it means to lead an animal out. Where damage is occasioned, both laws bind to compensation.

units.la: Pecus soli exposita, aut ineptis commendata. Pastor tenetur. Emolumentum perceptum compensatur; vel damnum totum. Ejus æstimatio. Annot. Non sufficit, concludere pecudem. Regula communis in pastore deficiens. Modus prior quo pecus in alterius horto deprehenditur. Modus alter. Isque majoris momenti. Damni æstimandi via aperitur. Matura fruges hic variant. Misna ex jure Rom. confirmata.
units.tr: Livestock left in the open field, or entrusted to the unskilled. The herdsman is liable. Profit received is set off, or else the whole loss. Its valuation. Annotation. It is not enough to shut in the animal. The common rule fails in the case of the herdsman. The first mode, by which an animal is caught in another's garden. The second mode, which is of greater weight. The way to estimate the damage is opened. Here the crops vary as they ripen. The Mishnah confirmed from Roman law.

units.la: Metam colligens in agro alterius. Ann. Ritus antiquus colligendi metam. Damnum inde ortum. Custos post datam ingrediendi veniam, obligatur. Casus Misnæ cum leg. Rom. collatus.
units.tr: Gathering a heap of cut crops in another's field. Annotation. The ancient rite of gathering the heap. The damage arising from it. A guard who, after being given leave to enter, is bound. The case of the Mishnah compared with the Roman law.

units.la: Incendiarii aliorum operâ utentes. Ventus si ignem suscitet. Incendiarius ad compensationem tenetur. Quid, si incendium longius serpat. Ann. Quinam judicio tantum cœlesti teneantur. Legis restrictio. Diversa Maimonidæ lectio in antiquissimo codice Nob. L. G. à Renesse. קפּס, quis. Videre voces. Postrema causa, de incendio tenetur. Ex. 22. 6. explicatur. כיר. Ad incendium alia multa revocantur. Quid, si quis hominem adurat. Incendiarius qui absolvatur. Viæ publicæ latitudo. De incendii multa ac pœna gravissima è leg. Rom.
units.tr: Incendiaries who use the labour of others. If the wind stirs up the fire. The incendiary is liable to compensation. What if the fire spreads further? Annotation. Who are liable to heavenly judgment alone. Restriction of the law. A different reading of Maimonides in the very ancient codex of Nob. L. G. à Renesse: קפּס [kapas], who. Observe the words. The last case: he is liable for the fire. Explained from Exodus 22:6. כיר [kir]. Many other things are referred to fire. What if someone burns a man? The incendiary who is acquitted. The breadth of the public way. On the great fine and most severe penalty for fire from Roman law.

units.la: Quousque incendium serpat sine culpa. Diversa sententiæ de compensandis iis quæ in meta conflagrant. De servo & hædo combusto casus diversi. De iis quæ ædibus conflagrantibus continentur. Ann. תעבור כדלוק, quid. Spatium atrii sacri. Ager vel locus Cori, item duarum Searum. Vbi tuto ignis accendatur. De eo sententia alia. Verum, incendii ratio ac modus considerandus est. Iudæorum sententia ex ff. Ad l. Aqu. confirmata. Aliquando ventus excusat incendiarium. Distinctè expenduntur quæ metâ dum conflagrat comprehenduntur. Quomodo accipiendum, conflagrante servo, absolvi incendiarium. Regula juris, קים לייה כדרכה מינויה.
units.tr: How far a fire may spread without fault. Differing opinions on compensating for things that burn up in the field. On the case of a burnt slave and a burnt kid, different cases. On the things contained in houses when they catch fire. Annotation. תעבור כדלוק [ta'avor kedoleq], what it means: "it shall pass through as a flame." The space of the sacred court. A field or place of Kor, likewise of two seahs. Where a fire may be lit safely. On this, another opinion. But the nature and manner of the fire must be considered. The opinion of the Jews, confirmed from the Digest, Ad legem Aquiliam. Sometimes the wind excuses the incendiary. The things that are caught up while the field is burning are weighed carefully. How it is to be understood, that the incendiary is acquitted when a slave is burning. The rule of law, קים לייה כדרכה מינויה [kim lei kidrakha minuyah]: he holds it in the way that he himself holds it.

units.la: Stric-tura à malleis fabrilibus dissiliens. Lino onustus camelus, quando dominum incendii reum faciat. Lucerna encaniorum privilegiaria.Ann. ¹ Quid sit ꝑ strictura. ² Incendium fortuitum magis excusant Romani. Casus pro negligentia in ff. Tres gradus in delicto. ³ Lucernam quando & quare loco periculoso ponere liceat. In fortuito incendio non exigi restitutionem, è Dig. & Cod. probatur.
units.tr: The stricture leaping from the smiths' hammers. When a camel laden with flax makes its owner liable for a fire. The lamp of the fullers, a privileged matter. Annotation. 1 What the stricture is. 2 The Romans excuse a chance fire more. Cases of negligence in the Digest. Three degrees of fault. 3 When and why it is lawful to set a lamp in a dangerous place. From the Digest and Code it is proved that in an accidental fire no restitution is exacted.

units.la: Modus rependendi duplum compar. cum restitutione quadrupli. Qui furatur à fure, qui se habeat. Ann. ¹ Ex.22.4.9.exponuntur. Dupli & quadrupli restitutio in eadem re. Ratio duplex exigendi in pecoribus quadruplum & quintuplum. Longe diversa multa, si quis invitus culpam agnoscat, quam si sponte fassus deprecetur culpam. Hinc conciliatur lex Ex. 22.1.9.cum Lev. 6.4.5. Itaque explicatur Lev.6. 4. & Num.5.7. Litera ¹ ꝑo si. Restitutio fortis cum quinta, quorum sit. Lev.4.22.23. explicatur. Voces quandoque agnitionem rei & professionem denotant. Ita expon. Ef. §8. 2. ex Chald. & Rab. Poenarum distinctio ex jure Rom. illustrata. Applicatio diversa. ² Causa quare minus rependat furans à fure. Secundum complures desperatio proprietarii rem furi acquirit. Exod. 22.7. ex mente Iud. exponitur. Fur secundus priori obligatur. Etiam secundum jus Romanum, ex cujusdam sententia.
units.tr: The manner of repaying double, compared with restitution of fourfold. He who steals from a thief, how he stands. Annotation. 1 Exodus 22:4, 9 explained. Restitution of double and of fourfold in the same thing. The twofold reason for exacting fourfold and fivefold in the case of livestock. Much is quite different if someone reluctantly acknowledges his fault, as opposed to one who voluntarily confesses and begs pardon for his fault. Hence the law of Exodus 22:1, 9 is reconciled with Leviticus 6:4–5. Thus Leviticus 6:4 and Numbers 5:7 are explained. The letter פ [pe], "if." Restitution of the principal with a fifth: to whom it belongs. Leviticus 4:22–23 explained. Words sometimes denote acknowledgment of a thing and a confession. So Isaiah 8:2 is explained from the Chaldee and the rabbis. The distinction of penalties illustrated from Roman law. A different application. 2 The reason why a thief repays less than a thief. According to several, the owner's despair gives the thief the thing. Exodus 22:7 explained according to the mind of the Jews. A second thief is bound to the first. Also according to Roman law, from the opinion of a certain author.

units.la: Furis actiones diversæ. Cum venditio, tum mactatio pecudis furtiva variis casibus distinguuntur: unde secundum quosdam jura diversa. Furatus à patre. Pecus furtiva discerpta. Ann. ¹ ꝑo aut. ² Regula'ꞏꞏ op, aliter exponitur. Minor poena in majori contineri censetur. ³ Idololatria poena. ⁴ Dies expiationis: & qui in furem tum mactantem animadvertatur. Regula, Vapulans non rependit. ⁵ Expenduntur furti casus diversi in filio. ⁶ Consecratio rei furtiva. In furto consecratorum mitiores injuste Ebraei. Exod. 22.9. vindicatur, Lev. 5.16. explicatur è Maim. ⁷ Utilitatem in furto expendunt Iudai. ⁸ Declarantur םיפס & נכלה. eorum species. 9 Profana & sanêta alieno loco mactata. עורפ. קדשי קדשים. Annuli mactationis. Comparantur Iudæi & Romani in pœna vel multa furti.
units.tr: The actions of a thief are different. When the sale, and also the slaughter of a stolen animal, are distinguished by various cases; hence, according to some, different laws apply. A man who steals from his father. A stolen animal torn in pieces. Annotation. 1 פ [pe], "or." 2 The rule of ... is explained otherwise. The lesser penalty is held to be contained in the greater. 3 The penalty for idolatry. 4 The Day of Atonement; and who is punished when he slaughters the thief. The rule: one who is beaten does not repay. 5 The different cases of theft in a son are weighed. 6 The consecration of a stolen thing. In theft, the Jews unjustly treat consecrated things more leniently. Exodus 22:9 is vindicated, Leviticus 5:16 explained from Maimonides. 7 The Jews weigh the advantage in theft. 8 The terms ספיס [sefasim?] and נכלה [nikhlah] are declared, and their kinds. 9 Holy and profane things slaughtered in another place. עורפ [ʿorfe], the neck-breaking; קדשי קדשים [kodshei kodashim], holy of holies. The rings of slaughter. The Jews and the Romans are compared in the penalty or fine for theft.

units.la: Testes incongrui de diversis furum actionibus, diversimode confiderantur. Testimonium irritum. An.1 Testes incongrui, & מוכחתי falsitatis convicti.2 Incongrui testis conditio ad quosvis mendaces extenda. Testes quando & quomodo totam furis pœnam sustineant. 3 Testes posteriores quando in triplum condemnentur.4 Fur duplum, testes triplum repêdentes.5 Quid si unus tantum testis falsi arguatur.6 Regula juris, מלמ מלבש. De teste uno; item falsario, ex Codice.
units.tr: Unsuitable witnesses concerning the different actions of thieves are considered in different ways. Invalid testimony. Annotation. 1 Unsuitable witnesses, and those convicted of falsehood, מוכחתי [mukhahti]. 2 The condition of an unsuitable witness is extended to any liars. When and how witnesses bear the whole penalty of the thief. 3 When later witnesses are condemned to triple. 4 A thief repays double, witnesses repaying triple. 5 What if only one witness is convicted of falsehood? 6 The rule of law, מלמ מלבש [malmah malbish]. Concerning one witness; likewise a forger, from the Code.

units.la: Si ipse fur sit testis solus. Sabbatho mactata pecus furtiva. Consecratio pecudis furtiva. Sancta pro quibus alia substituenda. Ann.1 Regula, מורם בקטן. fassus injuriam vel cujus nomine multam debet, liber est. Fur rem furtivam cum quinta rependens.2 Idolo mactata pecus. Supplicium capitale quomodo multam absorbeat.3 Pecus patri erepta, & post mortem mactata.4 Injusta in consecratis sententia.5 Quid נדבות. Mactatio legitima reatum inducens. Romani in tentantes privata sacra severiores Ebræis. §. 5.
units.tr: If the thief himself is the sole witness. A stolen animal slaughtered on the Sabbath. Consecration of a stolen animal. Holy things for which another must be substituted. Ann. Rule: the lesser is lifted up from the greater [מורם בקטן]. One who confesses an injury, or for whom a fine is owed, is free. A thief who repays the stolen thing with a fifth. An animal slaughtered for an idol. How capital punishment absorbs the fine. An animal snatched from its father and slaughtered after his death. An unjust sentence concerning consecrated things. What are the freewill offerings [נדבות]. Lawful slaughter that induces guilt. The Romans were harsher than the Hebrews toward those who attempted private sacred rites. §. 5.

units.la: Venditio qualis rei furtiva non puniatur. De pecude furtiva, qua vitiose mactatur. Loca ubi furtum fit, mactatio, & venditio, jus immutant. Ann.1 Scripturam qui enarrent Iudæi. Ps. 68. 21. quam ridicule accipiant; Ex. 22. 1. insulsè restringant. ubi eorundem trica.2 Quid è Deut. 14. 21. inepte eliciant.3 מוחר variis modis exponitur.4 מתקך. Male Scrip. restringunt Ebræi.5 In æstimando furto dissentiunt Rom. & Ebr. Contrectationis effectum. §. 6.
units.tr: How the sale of a stolen thing is not punished. Concerning a stolen animal that is slaughtered in a faulty manner. Places where theft occurs, slaughter, and sale alter the law. Ann. How the Jews expound Scripture. Ps. 68:21 is absurdly understood; Ex. 22:1 is foolishly restricted, where their trickery lies. What they absurdly draw out of Deut. 14:21. The word [מוחר] is explained in various ways. The word [מתקך] The Hebrews restrict Scripture wrongly. The Romans and the Hebrews disagree in estimating theft. The effect of handling. §. 6.

units.la: Quænam furtum constituant, quæ secus. ubi de re furtiva alteri data. An.1 קסה acquirere latè patet Ebræis. Modi transferendi sive acquirendi. ubi de traditione, inprimis Elevatione, Attratione. Quid hɔmp. Elevatione ubique rem transferri. Redemptio primogeniti. De tempore ejus. Quando Deo sistendus. Iesus quando & quare Ierosolymam allatus. Iudei à verbis Num. 18.16. recedunt. Quid in redemptionem detur. Voces conjunctas ad personas diversas etiam referri. Differentia hujus Misna à leg. Romanis.
units.tr: What constitutes theft and what does not; where a stolen thing has been given to another. Ann. The word [קסה] to acquire, is very widely applied by the Hebrews. Modes of transferring or acquiring. Where concerning delivery, especially by lifting up and by drawing. What [hɔmp.]. By lifting up, a thing is transferred everywhere. The redemption of the firstborn. Its time. When one must present oneself before God. When and why Jesus was brought to Jerusalem. The Jews depart from the words of Num. 18:16. What is given in redemption. Conjoined words may also refer to different persons. The difference of this Mishnah from the Roman laws.

units.la: Minuta pecora, gallinaceos, porcos, canes, ubi & an educare liceat. De reti columbarum. Quibus sylvis minuta pecora alere liceat. Quanta cura veteres caverint, ne quadrup. pauperiem faceret. Primorum verborum in Misna ratio. Superstitionis Iudaica exemplum è Talmude. Quo casu primum interdictum de minutis pecoribus, non obtineat. Statutorum Ebr. conditio. Causa quare Syria pro aliis regionibus veniat. 2 Sam. 8. v. 3.4. explicantur. Quæ fit Syria Tsobaa. Sophene ubi. Hamath. Palmyrena. Termini Israelis quousque. 2 Sam. 8. conciliatur cum 1 Chron 18. Scriptura S. quibus scripta. 2 Sam. 5. v. 8. explicatur. Ellipsis iterum probatur. Quare pecora minuta in Syria educare liceat. Babylonia cum Canaane confertur. Contaminandi modus. Quare arceantur gallinacei. Nulla sterquilinia Hierosolymis. Ierusalem decem gaudebat privilegiis. de iis ordine. Atque hac occasione de עיר הקדש civitate impulsa, & תומאה aliisque differitur. & quare hortos Ieruf. prohibeant: mortuosque eodem die sepeliant. Res sanctissimæ, & Sancta quæ vocant Levia: item de loco ubi eduntur. Qua sancta passim in terra Canaan ederentur. Hyrcani & Aristobuli dissidium. Origo interdicti de alendo porco. Iudais Græcorum scientiam discere non licebat. Porci etiam ad ungendum pelles, & mercaturam, non permissi. Cujus esus interdictus; etiam mercatura interdicta: cum exceptione duplici. De Matt. 8. 30. multis agitur. Extra tribum Iuda & Benjaminis, multi Israelita in terra Chanaan post captiv. Babyl. Christus tantum institutionem oralem & miracula Israelitis exhibuit. Israelitae reduces duorum generum. Neh. 8 1. quomodo intelligatur: 2 Chron. 34. 33. qui accipiatur. Israelitae etiam post Assyriacam captivitatem, in Chanaan erant. Israelitae, non tantum Iudaei, sub Cyro rediere. Hos. 1.6. cum aliis conciliatur. Chanaan plurimos alienigenas habuit in adventu Christi. Israelitae ultra Genezareth non adeo superstitiosi. Gadareni cujates essent. Daemoniaci Matt. 8.28. Quod de porcis, ad reliquas bestias interdictas extenditur. De canibus non alendis, vel catena saltem ligandis, sententia diversa: earumq; rationibus. Vbi eos solutos habere liceat. Nehardea, ubi sita. quid. Quibus conditionibus rete columbis tendere licitum. Conciliantur Misna quae pugnare videbantur. Romanis legibus Misna aequitas probatur.
units.tr: Small cattle, poultry, pigs, dogs: where and whether it is lawful to rear them. Concerning a dovecote net. In what woods it is lawful to feed small cattle. How carefully the ancients took care that a quadruped should not cause damage. The reason for the first words in the Mishnah. An example of Jewish superstition from the Talmud. In what case the first prohibition concerning small cattle does not hold. The condition of the Hebrew statutes. The reason why Syria is mentioned rather than other regions. 2 Sam. 8:3–4 is explained. What is Syria-Zobah. Where Sophene is. Hamath. Palmyrene. How far the borders of Israel extend. 2 Sam. 8 is reconciled with 1 Chron. 18. For whom Holy Scripture was written. 2 Sam. 5:8 is explained. An ellipsis is again proved. Why it is lawful to rear small cattle in Syria. Babylonia is compared with Canaan. The manner of contamination. Why poultry are excluded. No dunghills in Jerusalem. Jerusalem enjoyed ten privileges, discussed in order. And on this occasion there is a digression on the holy city [עיר הקדש], on uncleanness [תומאה] and other matters; and why they forbid gardens in Jerusalem, and bury the dead on the same day. The most holy things, and the things called holy of the lesser grade, namely the Levites; also concerning the place where they are eaten. Which holy things were eaten everywhere in the land of Canaan. The quarrel of Hyrcanus and Aristobulus. The origin of the prohibition on rearing pigs. The Jews were not permitted to learn the wisdom of the Greeks. Pigs were also not permitted for anointing with their skins, nor for trade. Whose eating was forbidden; trade was also forbidden, with a twofold exception. Many matters are discussed concerning Matt. 8:30. Outside the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, many Israelites remained in the land of Canaan after the Babylonian captivity. Christ gave only oral instruction and miracles to the Israelites. The returning Israelites were of two kinds. How Neh. 8:1 is to be understood; what is meant by 2 Chron. 34:33. The Israelites were also in Canaan after the Assyrian captivity. Not only Jews but Israelites returned under Cyrus. Hos. 1:6 is reconciled with other passages. Canaan had very many foreigners at the coming of Christ. The Israelites beyond Gennesaret were not so superstitious. Whose people the Gadarenes were. The demoniacs of Matt. 8:28. What is said about pigs is extended to the other forbidden animals. Concerning not feeding dogs, or at least keeping them chained, there is a differing opinion, and the reasons for them. Where it is lawful to keep them loose. Nehardea, where it lies, and what it is. On what conditions it is lawful to set a net for doves. The Mishnah passages that seemed to conflict are reconciled. The equity of the Mishnah is proved from Roman laws.

units.la: Qui vitiat alterum, quinque nominibus tenetur. ubi ordine de damno corpori illato, dolore, curatione, cessatione, & ignominia, etiam fortuita Ann. Ex. 21. 24. & Lev. 24. 20. enarrantur. Itaque Talionis lex defenditur: & qui accipiatur oculus pro oculo, &c. expenditur. De Num. 35. 31. comm. Ex. 21. 25. contra Iudaeos vindicatur. Quid pr Ex. 21 19. Poena corporalis in pecuniariam mutata. In vitio illato compensando, omnes laesos pro servis habebant. Talio ex Leg 12. Tab. & Cod. Talionis lex revocata. Dum talio vigeret, corporalis poena etiam in pecuniariam mutata. Talionis aequitas ex Gellio. Modus quo aestimatur dolor compensandus. Ex. 21. 25. ex mente Gem. expositus. Actionem in alterum dari ob dolorem illatum, ex jure Romano. Cessationis compensatio extenditur. pr quid Ex. 21. v. 19. ex Gem. Gemaram a Misna differentire, in plaga recrudescente. Varia consideranda & quae, in cessatione compensanda. Cessationem praestandam & curationis impendia, censent jura Rom. Ignominiam pro conditione perf. diversa luendam, ratione etiam probatur. Nudus quis dicatur. Orientalium vestes. Gradibus ad altare cur non ascendendu. Ignominia non animadversa vindicatur. Deut. 25. 11, 12. enarrantur è Magistris. Manus amputanda redimi potuit. Qua de ignominia vindicanda, ejusque incremento dicta, ex Rom. leg. confirmantur: & injuriam vindicandam, quam etiam infert qui in aliam personam collimabat.
units.tr: One who injures another is liable under five heads: namely, damage done to the body, pain, cure, loss of work, and disgrace, even if accidental. Ann. Ex. 21:24 and Lev. 24:20 are set out. Thus the law of talion is defended, and the phrase "eye for eye" and so on is weighed. Num. 35:31 is compared with Ex. 21:25, and is vindicated against the Jews. What is to be said on Ex. 21:19. Corporal punishment was changed into a pecuniary one. In compensating for an injury inflicted, they regarded all who were harmed as slaves. Talion from the Law of the Twelve Tables and the Code. The law of talion was revoked. While talion was in force, corporal punishment was also changed into a pecuniary one. The equity of talion, from Gellius. The manner in which the pain to be compensated is estimated. Ex. 21:25 is explained according to the intention of the Gemara. That an action is given against another on account of pain inflicted, from Roman law. The compensation for loss of work is extended. What is meant by Ex. 21:19, from the Gemara. The Gemara differs from the Mishnah in the case of a wound that breaks open again. Various things to be considered, and which, in compensating for loss of work. Roman laws hold that loss of work and the expenses of cure are to be paid. Disgrace is to be paid according to the different condition of the person, which is also proved by reason. Who is to be called naked. The garments of the Orientals. Why one should not ascend to the altar by steps. Disgrace not punished is avenged. Deut. 25:11–12 is set out from the teachers. A hand that deserved amputation could be redeemed. Concerning the vindication of disgrace and its increase, these points are confirmed from Roman law; and the injury that one inflicts even on a different person at whom he aimed is to be avenged.

units.la: Confertur damnum ab homine datum, cum eo quod ejus bos dedit. De pretio excussi fœtus. Ann. Ex. 21. 22. varie enarratur. Lasio fortuita. Pœna homicidii defenditur. Ita lex talionis in genere. De ejus incommodis. item redemptione pœna. Abortionis auctor, ex jure aliarum gentium, qui plectendus. De ejectio fœtus, ut & pauperiei multa, contra Iudæos. approbante jure Romano. §. 3.
units.tr: The damage done by a man is compared with the damage done by his ox. On the price of an aborted foetus. Exodus 21:22 is variously explained. Accidental harm. The penalty for homicide is defended. So the law of retaliation in general, and its drawbacks; likewise the redemption of a penalty. The author of an abortion, by the law of other nations, is to be punished, and likewise the expulsion of a foetus; also the fine for poverty, against the Jews, with the approval of Roman law. §. 3.

units.la: Quinam ad quintuplam illam multam §.1 teneantur. Quando cessatio non compensetur. De ignominia servorum. Ann. Misna lectio diversa. Iudaei contradicunt legi Ex. 21. 15. adeoque verberantem parentes à morte absolvunt. Contra si ex errore occidat, morte multant. Superstitiosi, dum filio ne patri venam secet, &c. interdicunt. De eo qui expiationis die vitiat proximum. Qui eo die opus facit, plagis cædendus. Vapulans à multa pecuniaria absolvitur; & qui hanc solvit, à verberibus. Lev. 24. 20 acute expositus à Iud. De eo qui proprio servo vitium corporis infert. Ex. 21. 26. vindicatur contra Iudæos. De loco Lev. 24. 19. Cananaeus. Alterius servo Ebræo manum amputantis multa. Misna cum Ex. 21. 26. conciliatur. Vir cum fratre, quid Deut 25. 11. Parentes contra filios, servi contra dominos proprios ac alienos defenduntur, legibus Romanorum.
units.tr: Who are liable to the fivefold fine of §. 1. When a cessation of work is not compensated. On the disgrace of slaves. Annotation: the Mishnah reading differs. The Jews contradict the law of Exodus 21:15, and so absolve from death those who strike their parents. On the contrary, if someone kills by mistake, they punish him with death. The superstitious forbid a son to let blood from his father, etc. On one who wounds his neighbour on the Day of Atonement. One who works on that day is to be beaten with stripes. One who is beaten is released from a money fine, and one who pays this fine is released from the stripes. Leviticus 24:20 is acutely expounded by the Jews. On one who inflicts a bodily injury on his own slave. Exodus 21:26 is vindicated against the Jews. On the passage Leviticus 24:19. The Canaanite. The fine for one who cuts off the hand of another's Hebrew slave. The Mishnah is reconciled with Exodus 21:26. A husband with his brother: what of Deuteronomy 25:11? Parents against children, and slaves against their own and others' masters, are defended by the laws of the Romans.

units.la: Surdi, fatui, pupilli, servi, marita conditio potior in compensando corporis vitio. Ann. Misna lectio diversa. Natura vitia & imbecillitas ætatis, quos peccantes absolvat. Marita & servus peccantes quare cum jam immunes sint, postea, multentur. Quid ais? Dotem illatam quando repetat uxor; quando maritus obtineat. De servis reis & maritatis, quomodo Rom. & Ebr. leges differant & conveniant.
units.tr: The condition of the deaf, the foolish, the minors, the slaves, and the married woman is more favourable in compensating for a bodily defect. Annotation: the Mishnah reading differs. The nature of the defect and the weakness of age, which excuse those who offend. Why a married woman and a slave, who offend, are punished afterwards, although they were already exempt. What do you say? When a wife may reclaim her dowry, and when the husband keeps it. On slaves and married women who are accused, how the Roman and Hebrew laws differ and agree.

units.la: Percutiens patrem, & vitians alterum in sabbatho, vel denique servum suum Cananaeum. Ann.¹ Quanam fuerit capitis poena, si quis in parente vibicem extitasset. Si filia id faciat.² Regula, Corrumpens quid die sabbathi, à morte immunis: cum exceptione sua.³ Exod. 21. 26. ad quosvis servos, contra Iudaeorum sententiam, extenditur.
units.tr: Striking a father, and wounding another on the Sabbath, or finally one's own Canaanite slave. Annotation: what the capital penalty would have been if someone had left a weal on a parent. If a daughter does this. The rule: one who corrupts something on the Sabbath is immune from death, with its exception. Exodus 21:26 is extended to all slaves whatever, against the opinion of the Jews.

units.la: Varia multa proponuntur, si quis alteri colaphum, alapam impingat, aures vellat, evellat capillos, conspuat quem, pallium detrahat, denudet caput mulieris. Quia quis sibi impune facit, aliis facta vindicari. Ann.¹ תוקף לחביר variis modis exponitur. quid sit secundum variorum sententias. ejus multa. ut etiam trudentis genu, & calcitrantis. De colaphis Christo impactis.⁴ לפו, לפר. Siclus Iudaicus duplo major Galilaeo. Siclus alius Tyrius; alius provincialis: ubi de utriusque diverfissimo valore. Moneta argentea Legis; & magistrorum. Matth. 5. 26. Graecus & Syrus, ex Talmude conciliantur expedita ratione. λεπτὰ Marc. 12. 42. Quadrantem esse multiplicem. דרוך cujus valoris. non esse ἀσσάριον. Quid ἀσσάριον Matth. 10. 29. & Luc. 12. 6. nempe ערכ; cujus valor ex antiquis. Hesychius corrector. Unde aestimandi Ebr. nummi.⁵ מטר, quid. Alapa Christo infracta. παρειά quid in passionis historia. Malas meas depilantibus, Esa. 50. v. 6. ex Euang. Christo applicatur. δίφρος quid Luc. 22. 63. significat.⁶ כוס tribus modis exponitur. Quaecunque dedecora vindicanda censuerunt Iudei, iis Christum assecere. Vestem aliquoties Christo detractam. In dedecore & insamia vindicanda spectandam esse laesi conditionem: etiam secundum Ius Rom. e quo Misna comprobatur.
units.tr: Many varied cases are set forth: if someone strikes another with a fist or a slap, pulls his ears, plucks out his hair, spits on someone, strips off his cloak, or uncovers a woman's head. Because what someone does to himself with impunity, he is punished for doing to others. Annotation: the expression תוקף לחביר is explained in various ways; what it means according to the opinions of various writers, and its many [meanings], as also of the one who pushes with the knee and of the one who kicks. On the blows struck upon Christ. לפו, לפר. The Jewish shekel was double the Galilean. Another shekel, the Tyrian; another, the provincial: where there is a very great difference in the value of each. The silver coin of the Law and of the teachers. Matthew 5:26. The Greek and the Syriac are reconciled from the Talmud by a ready explanation. λεπτά, Mark 12:42. The quadrans was of several kinds. דרוך, of what value. It was not the ἀσσάριον. What the ἀσσάριον is in Matthew 10:29 and Luke 12:6, namely ערכ; its value from the ancients. Hesychius the corrector. From what [standard] Hebrew coins are to be valued. מטר, what it is. The blow struck upon Christ. What παρειά means in the account of the Passion. Esaias 50:6, "to them that pulled off the hair," is applied to Christ from the Gospel. What δίφρος means in Luke 22:63. כוס is explained in three ways. Whatever insults the Jews judged to require punishment, they inflicted upon Christ. His garment was taken from him on several occasions. In vindicating dishonour and infamy, the condition of the injured party is to be considered, also according to Roman law, by which the Mishnah is confirmed.

units.la: Ladentem praeter multam, ad petendam remissionem teneri. Lenitas ejus qui propitiandus est. Ei qui se laedi praecipit, quo casu impune mos geratur. Iussum etiam alteri male facere, teneri. Ann. 1 Peccati veniam expetendam è Talmude asseritur. idque cum Christi doctrina confertur. Sacerdotii Christi partes.2 Facilitas in remittendis peccatis in Talmude docetur, eodem modo, quo eam Servator exigit.3 Volenti fieri injuriam. Id ratione addita restringunt Iudaei.4 Si quis sibi pedem frangi jubeat, qui accipiendum. Canon, [Hebrew]. 5 In bonis externis secus se rem habere. ubi non pro ita, Obadia de Bart. 6 Cujus sit, spondere absolutionem. 7 Perpetrantis peccatum levius, quam ejus qui damnum dari jubet. De peccato jussu alterius commisso, quid leges Romanae decernant.
units.tr: One who strikes [another], besides the fine, is bound to seek forgiveness. The gentleness of the one who is to be propitiated. In the case of one who orders himself to be harmed, in which case the wish may be carried out with impunity. One who orders another to do evil is also liable. Annotation: 1 The pardon of sin is asserted to be sought from the Talmud, and this is compared with the teaching of Christ. The parts of Christ's priesthood. 2 Facility in remitting sins is taught in the Talmud, in the same way as the Saviour requires it. 3 Volenti non fit iniuria. The Jews restrict this with an added reason. 4 If someone orders his foot to be broken, what is to be received. Canon, [Hebrew]. 5 In external goods the case is otherwise, where it is not so; Obadiah of Bertinoro. 6 Whose office it is to promise absolution. 7 The sin of the one who perpetrates is lighter than that of the one who orders the damage to be done. What Roman laws decree concerning a sin committed at another's command.
CAP. 9. §. I.

units.la: In rapto rependendo examinandum esse, quod fuerit pretium cum raperetur. Annot. 1 Definitio furti, item rapina. Levit. 6.4. 5. contra Iudaeos vindicantur. Ideoque de poena rapti. Quid [Hebrew].
units.tr: In restoring what was seized, it must be examined what the price was when it was seized. Annotation. 1 The definition of theft, and likewise of robbery. Leviticus 6:4, 5 is vindicated against the Jews. And so on the penalty for the seized thing. What [Hebrew].

units.la: 2 Materia rapta, non quod ex ea fit, consideranda. 3 Similiter in vacca spectatur, quod pretium fuerit cum raperetur.4 Adeoque si postea foeta reddatur, foetus non attenditur. Ita in ove, quae fit lanigera. In damno leges Rom. etiam tempus expendunt. & severius in raptum, quam furtum animadvertunt; Iudaei contra. §. 2.
units.tr: 2 The material seized, not what is made from it, is to be considered. 3 Similarly in the case of a cow, what the price was when it was seized is considered. 4 And so if it is afterwards returned pregnant, the offspring is not taken into account. So too with a sheep that becomes woolly. In damage, Roman laws also weigh the time, and punish robbery more severely than theft; the Jews, on the contrary, [do otherwise]. §. 2.

units.la: Quomodo rapti compensatio instituatur, si res rapta melior facta fuerit in raptoris manu. Item, si res deterior facta sit: vel plane inutilis reddita fuerit. Ann. 1 Servi quando aquentur mobilibus, quando fundis. De rapto in raptoris manu immutato, sententia Maim. 2 Quis nummus [Hebrew] & [Hebrew], ex mente diversorum. Putrescere, cujus in Mishna mentio. Quanam inscriptio numi Hierosolymitani. 3 [Hebrew]. Utilitas raptoris in compensatione spectetur. Iniquum Iud. judicium. Vitium bestia non ita obest ante latam sententiam.
units.tr: How the compensation for what was seized is to be arranged, if the seized thing has become better in the hand of the robber; likewise, if the thing has become worse, or has been rendered wholly useless. Annotation. 1 When slaves are equated with movables, and when with estates. On the thing seized, changed in the robber's hand, the opinion of Maimonides. 2 What coin [Hebrew] and [Hebrew] is, according to the opinions of various writers. To rot away, which is mentioned in the Mishnah. What the inscription of the Jerusalem coin is. 3 [Hebrew]. The advantage of the robber is to be considered in the compensation. An unfair Jewish judgement. A beast's defect does not harm [the owner] before sentence is passed.

units.la: Fabri qui novum quid parandum, vel aliquid ad reparandum acceperunt, qui de corruptione teneantur. Similiter architectus, qui destruendo parietem, damnum dedit. s quid in hac lege. De fabro etiam agi qui novi quid faciendum in se suscepit, probatur è Gem. & Maim. Immutatio rei, quando transferat dominium. מגרל, quid. Locatori etiam consuli, & damnum esse conductoris, secundum leges Romanas. Vbi & de eo qui transportandam rem conduxit.
units.tr: Craftsmen who have undertaken to make something new, or to repair something, and who are liable for spoilage. Likewise the architect who, by pulling down a wall, caused damage. Whether anything is said in this law. That the craftsman who undertook to make something new is also dealt with is proved from the Gemara and Maimonides. A change in a thing, when it transfers ownership. Migral (מגרל): what it is. That the one who hired out the work should also be considered, and the loss falls on the one who hired, according to Roman laws. Here also concerning the one who hired a thing to be carried.

units.la: Insector si lanam adurat, fusco colore fædet, aliove colore inficiat, quam debebat; quid præstet. יוח cortina, quid. כפור. כפורת דודי. כלבוס. Infectoris conditio deterior, quam locatoris. Quid ידו על התחתונה. Pretium lana alio colore tincta, quam oportebat, non persolvi. Immutatio contra communiorem regulam, hic rem non alienat. conductorem locatori præstare de quo convenit, etiam ex leg. Rom.
units.tr: A dyer who scorches wool, stains it with a dark colour, or dyes it with another colour than he ought, and what he owes. Yoach (יוח): a curtain, what it is. Kapporeth (כפור), the "kapporet of my beloved." Kalbos (כלבוס). The dyer's position is worse than the hirer's. What "yado al ha-tachtonah" (ידו על התחתונה) means. The price of wool dyed with another colour than it should have been is not paid. This is a change against the more common rule, since here he does not alienate the thing. The contractor owes the one who hired him what was agreed, also according to Roman law.

units.la: Pejerans raptum ad proprietarium deferre tenetur in loca remotissima. Cui, ipsius loco, tradere liceat. מרומ cujus valoris. & יסף. Lev. 6. 5. explicatur. Horrenda delicta etiam hostiis expiata fuisse. Privati מלים varia species. ubi de pararo & infligitore. Iudaos dissonantia tradere. De generis convenientia apud Ebr. Quis, מליח ניכור, & מלים כית דין. Stator curia. Recuperator. Coactor. Quando huic raptum reddidisse sufficiat. Raptorem dupli restitutione multant leges Roman. etiamsi rem suam esse putavit.
units.tr: One who swears falsely must bring the stolen thing back to its owner, even to the most remote places. To whom it may be handed over in his place. Marom (מרום): of what value. And yasaf (יסף), explained at Lev. 6.5. Even horrible crimes were expiated by sacrifices. Milim (מלים), a varied kind; here concerning the pararo and the one who inflicts. The Jews hand over with disagreement. On the agreement of kind among the Hebrews: who... "nikhur" (ניכור) and "beth din" (כית דין) are the terms. The stator of the court. The recuperator. The coactor. When it suffices to have restored the stolen thing. Roman laws fine the robber with double restitution, even if he thought the thing was his own.

units.la: Quibus casibus raptor proprietarium in loca remota sequi non debeat; quo vero casu debeat. Ebrai docent quæ non consentiunt. ubi denuo de Lev.6.5. & syntaxi Ebraorum agitur. Minus valore minuti raptorem sublevat. De pœna rapti; etiam ex jure Canonico.
units.tr: In which cases the robber need not follow the owner to remote places, and in which case he must. The Hebrews teach things that do not agree. Here again Lev. 6.5 and the syntax of the Hebrews are discussed. A lesser value lightens the burden of the robber. On the penalty for robbery, also from the Canon law.

units.la: Quintam de quinta rapti &c. exigentes, quousque descendant.
units.tr: Those demanding the fifth of the fifth of the stolen thing, and so on, how far down they go.

units.la: Depositarii sponte fatentis multa. Ann. Quænam Lev.6.5. quinta solvenda dicatur. Ejus exemplum: & Maimonida sphalma. Scriptura contradicunt Iudai, de quo & sept. nota. Multa Ebraorum numismata valore suo æstimantur. ut רוינ, פרוסט, מטע, קונטרין, ἀσάλγοι, פטפם. Misna diversa lectio. Quid sit Lev.6.2.7. varie exponitur. פ&ב & בוא. Luc. 3.14. συκοφαντῶν. συκοφάντησα in Aristophane, συκοφάντης. Raptor quando minus multetur. Persona loquentes quando reticeantur. qua occasione de causa obscuritatis in Gemara. In depositarium quid decernant leges civ. Rom. in eum qui mutuum intervertit, vel commodatum. inque eum qui mercedem detinet. item qui rem perditam lucri causa sustulit. Disputatur de perjurii pæna ex leg. civili Rom.
units.tr: The fine of a depositary who voluntarily confesses. Annotation. What Lev. 6.5 says is to be paid as the fifth. An example of it, and a slip of Maimonides. The Jews contradict Scripture, on which the Septuagint also note. Many Hebrew coins are valued by their worth, such as ruin (רוינ), prust, mata, kontrin, asalgoi, patpam. A different reading in the Mishnah. What Lev. 6.2.7 means is variously explained. Peh and bet, and bo. Luke 3.14, sykophantōn. Sykophantēsa in Aristophanes; sykophantēs. When the robber is fined less. When the speaking persons are left unnamed, and on what occasion, because of the cause of obscurity in the Gemara. What the Roman civil laws decree against a depositary; against one who misapplies a loan or a commodatum; and against one who withholds wages; likewise against one who took away a lost thing for gain. The penalty for perjury is disputed from Roman civil law.

units.la: Depositarius si furetur, quantum debeat: si sponte fateatur, quæ sit multa. Ann. An si depositum adhuc integrum sit, duplum exigatur, cum occultatum fuit. Exodi 22.9. expenditur. פח synecdochice pro juramento.
units.tr: A depositary who steals, how much he owes; if he voluntarily confesses, what the fine is. Annotation. Whether, if the deposit is still intact, double is exacted when it was concealed. Exodus 22.9 is weighed. Pach (פח), used synecdochically for oath.

units.la: Surripiens quid patri suo, qui postea moriatur. Raptor ad solvendum mutuatus. Annot. Superstitio Iudaorum in explicando Levit. 6. 4. commate. An Misna verba בנו, filiis raptoris raptum restitui postulent. Haredibus proprietarii restituendum raptum, docent l. civiles Rom. Quo fundamento & quando fratribus illius restitui, præcipiant Iudai.
units.tr: One who steals something from his father, who afterwards dies. A robber who borrowed in order to pay. Annotation. The superstition of the Jews in explaining the clause of Lev. 6.4. Whether the words of the Mishnah, "his son," ask that the stolen thing be restored to the robber's sons. Roman civil laws teach that the stolen thing is to be restored to the heirs of the owner; on what foundation, and when, the Jews order it to be restored to his brothers.

units.la: Quid agendum, si parens voto bona sua interdicat filio. Ann. קונס quid. סומיפ. סמיפ. Inhumanitas parentum in liberos; & liberorum in parentes. Magis honorandi præceptores quam parentes, ex Ebr. mente. Libertas parentis postponenda libertati præceptoris. Duplex ratio interdicendi bona. Quomodo exhæredatus restituere bona dicatur. Nepos qui hæres. Unde exhæredatus sibi de necessariis prospiciat. Quomodo creditor mutuans exhaeredato, suum recuperet. Exheredationi liberorum cancellos ponunt leg. Rom. imo & sectioni bonorum paternorum. Patris esse liberis prospicere, è Xenophonte & V. Max.
units.tr: What is to be done if a parent, by vow, forbids his goods to his son. Annotation. Qons (קונס): what it is. Simifa (סומיפ), semif (סמיפ). The inhumanity of parents toward children, and of children toward parents. In the Hebrew view, teachers are to be honoured more than parents. The parent's liberty is to be set behind the liberty of the teacher. A twofold reason for forbidding goods. How a disinherited person is said to restore goods. A grandson who is heir. How a disinherited person provides himself with necessities. How a creditor who lends to the disinherited person recovers his own. Roman laws set limits on disinheriting children, and indeed also on the division of paternal goods. That it is a father's duty to provide for his children, from Xenophon and Valerius Maximus.
§. II.

units.la: Pradatus à peregrino, qui postea moritur. Pecunia peregrino surrepta, raptoris filiis quando cedat. Ann. Qua lege peregrino sint haeredes. Injustitia Iudaeorum. Num. 5.8. vindicatur. Reatus quid. Altera injustitia magistrorum. Quando raptoris fiant bona peregrino erepta. Quid fiat consecrata pecude post mortem domini. Pretio consecrata pecudis posteaque vendita, quid fiat. in quo differant. Maimonides restitutus. Codex Maimonida. Sacrificia quaedam non imperata. Quid. pp.
units.tr: Plundered by a foreigner who afterwards dies. Money taken from a foreigner: when it passes to the robber's sons. Annotation. By what law foreigners are heirs. The injustice of the Jews. Num. 5.8 is vindicated. What guilt is. Another injustice of the magistrates. When the goods snatched from a foreigner become the robber's. What is done with a consecrated animal after the owner's death. What happens to the price of a consecrated animal that was afterwards sold, and how the cases differ. Maimonides restored. The Code of Maimonides. Certain sacrifices not commanded: what they are. pp.

units.la: Raptor si ante oblatam victimam moriatur, quid data jam pecunia fiat. Reatus & raptum diversis facerd. classibus data. Reatus ante allatam rapinā non expiat: tamen ante quintam ipsius. Ann. Num. 5. v.10. vindicatur contra Iudaeos, & exponitur. Nomina virorum pro similibus accepta. Raptum & victimam ejus diversis tradere licuisse. Raptorem casu quodam secundam victimam attulisse. Futuri in consignificando vis. Non esse hic rapti & quintae ejus rationem eandem.
units.tr: If the robber dies before the victim is offered, what happens to the money already given. Guilt and the stolen thing were given to different classes. Guilt does not expiate before the stolen thing is restored, yet it does before its fifth is paid. Annotation. Num. 5 v. 10 is vindicated against the Jews and explained. Men's names are taken for similar ones. It was lawful to give the stolen thing and its victim to different persons. The robber by some chance brought a second victim. The force of the future in co-signifying. The reason for the stolen thing and for its fifth is not the same here.

units.la: Quando raptorum filii rependere teneantur. Publicanorum, & quaestorum arariorum arcae reprobatae. Annot. Synecdoche Misnica. Misna à magistris rejecta. etenim liberos raptorum semper obligari: nisi rapta comesta sint. Mobilia creditori opignerari. Desperationis vis in mutando dominio. Simile ex jure Romano. quid. ubi de evictione rei in fundo vendito. Nummos permutandi causa. quid. Publicanorum diffiniutio & patria. quid fit. Luc. 3.13. ex Talmud. illustratus. quis sit. De publicanorum & quaestorum numis, quos in aedibus habent. Quosve alibi extra arcam suam publicam habent. De raptorum liberis ex jure Rom.
units.tr: When the sons of robbers are bound to make restitution. The chests of the publicans and of the treasury quaestors rejected. Note. Mishnaic synecdoche. The Mishnah rejected by the teachers. For the children of robbers are always liable, unless the stolen goods have been eaten. Movables are pledged to the creditor. The force of despair in changing ownership. A similar case from Roman law. What? Where concerning the eviction of a thing in an estate that has been sold. Coins exchanged for the sake of exchange. What? The definition and homeland of publicans. What it is. Luke 3.13 illustrated from the Talmud. Who it is. Concerning the coins of publicans and quaestors, which they keep in their houses, or which they hold elsewhere outside their public chest. Concerning the children of robbers under Roman law.

units.la: Raptum tibi pro re erepta datum, fieri tuum. In aliis multis desperationem manifestam praerequiri. Repetentem sua, si laedat alium, teneri. Ann. יופ, שמו רמזו. & quomodo ex eorum fundamento, raptum ad tertium translatum, ipsius fiat. Nam domini translationem etiam rem alienare. Conciliatio Misnæ, ex latronum distinctione. Cuthai. Iudicare כתומדנכ. Evictionem praecidi derelictione, ex leg. Rom. Apum examen qui occupantis fiat: apium fera natura; non gallinarum: etiam ex jure Rom. Testimonium mulieris & pupilli. Amplius de eo qui sua repetit cum alterius damno. Misna cum jure Rom. confertur.
units.tr: A thing seized by robbery, given in exchange for a thing taken away, becomes yours. In many other cases a manifest desperation must be required beforehand. One who reclaims his own property, if he harms another in doing so, is bound to make restitution. Ann. [יופ, שמו רמזו]. And how, on the basis of their principle, a robbed thing transferred to a third party becomes his. For the owner's transfer also alienates the thing. Reconciliation of the Mishnah, from the distinction among robbers. Cuthai. To judge [כתומדנכ]. Eviction is cut off by abandonment, from the law of Rome. Whose a swarm of bees becomes by occupation: bees are of wild nature, not like hens; also from Roman law. The testimony of a woman and of a ward. Further, concerning one who reclaims his own goods to another's loss. The Mishnah is compared with Roman law.

units.la: Quando emptor rei furtivae pretium recipiat: quando rem furtivam retineat. An. Conditiones in recipienda re furtiva. Plerosq; evictionem rei in furto concedere; alios, proprietario pretium restituendu. פוס פקיפ, quid: de quo & tertia nota. Ementem a noto fure, rem gratis restituere; alii, proprietario restituendum pretium. Rem furtivam postquam dominus animu recup. despondit, non restituendam. Maimonida tribui sententias contrarias. Rei furtivae retentio & restitutio ex jure civ. Roman. In quo, rei furtivae pretium a venditore exigi. Eodem jure, rei furtivae persecutionem habere dominum. Recipiens rem furtivam, an pretium solutum rependat, ex l. civ. Roman. Rem furtivam pignori datam nonnisi reddita pecunia recipi, contra jus civ.Rom. praecipiunt Magistri. ppb. Phrasis שימו כל פ fuse exponitur. Negatio universali particula praepositia. Vox non tam rem, quam rei significata debitum denotans. Lex Num. 35. 28. ad Christum relata. In Rabboth qui illustretur Gen. 11. 4.
units.tr: When the buyer of stolen goods may receive the price, and when he may keep the stolen goods. Yes. The conditions for recovering stolen goods. Most authorities concede that the buyer must give up the goods in a theft; others hold that the price must be repaid to the owner. The phrase פוס פקיפ [pus pakip], what it means, on which see also a third note. If someone has bought from a known thief, he must return the goods free of charge; others hold that the price must be repaid to the owner. Stolen goods are not to be returned once the owner has given up the intention of recovering them. The contrary opinions are attributed to Maimonides. The retention and restitution of stolen goods under the civil law of Rome. In what case the price of stolen goods is demanded from the seller. By the same law the owner has an action to pursue stolen goods. Whether one who receives stolen goods may set off the price paid, under the civil law of Rome. The Masters order that stolen goods given in pledge may be received only once the money has been repaid, contrary to the civil law of Rome. ppb. The phrase שימו כל פ [shimu kol p] is explained at length. A universal negation by means of a preposition. The word denotes not so much the thing as the debt signified by the thing. Num. 35. 28 is related to Christ. In the Rabboth, what is illustrated by Gen. 11. 4.

units.la: Effusso vino suo colligens mel alterius effusum. Asinum eripiens alterius, negletto proprio. Ann. נסדר. Quae uno impetu effunduntur, occupantis fieri. Pactus pretium vini quis censeatur. Qua ratio ut quis ab absente domino bestiae pretium stipulatus censeatur.4 De סמן, mina, ex Ebr. Grac. & Lat. mina Tyria & provincialis. Minam communem pendere libram Colonienfem. Siclus. Aurei 2 Chron. 9. 16. μνᾶ diversi valoris Hefychio. Drachma Attica. Obolus. Denarius. Chalcus. Ærei asses. Mina statim post captivitatem usitata. Denarius posterioris templi. Sicli Ezech. 45. 12. Kimchi in voce סמן restitutus. Si quis alterius negotium gessit, quatenus damnum & sumptus restituantur, ex jur. civ. Rom. Restitutionem ab exitu dependere contra illud, statuit Maim.
units.tr: Someone who gathers another's honey poured out together with his own wine. Someone who rescues another's ass while neglecting his own. Note: [נסדר]. Things poured out in one rush belong to whoever seizes them. Whether a man who has agreed on a price for wine is to be regarded as having sold it. On what reasoning a man who has agreed on a price for an animal with the absent owner is to be regarded as having stipulated for it. On [סמן], the mina: from the Hebrew, Greek and Latin; the Tyrian and provincial mina. The common mina weighs a Cologne pound. The shekel. Gold coins: 2 Chron. 9:16. The mina of differing value according to Hesychius. The Attic drachma. The obol. The denarius. The chalcus. Bronze asses. The mina was in use immediately after the captivity. The denarius of the later temple. Shekels: Ezek. 45:12. Kimchi restored in the word [סמן]. If someone has managed another's affair, how far his loss and expenses are to be restored, from the Roman civil law. That restitution depends on the outcome, the Rambam decided, contrary to that law.

units.la: Cujus periculo surreptus ager reddatur deterior, raptoris, an proprietarii. Ann.1 Misna lectio diversa. ppפ, ex Gemara. Talmudista inepti grammatici. 2 Ereptum fundum semper primi domini censeri: idque cum jure Rom. confertur. Quare fundi calamitas hostilis sit proprietarii, non raptoris: & quando.3 Cur inundatio periculo proprietarii fiat. Quod raptoris culpa in agro suo quis patitur, id a raptore reparandum, leg. Rom.
units.tr: Whose risk it is when a field stolen away is returned in worse condition, the robber's or the owner's. Note: the reading of the Mishnah differs. [ppפ], from the Gemara. The Talmudist is an inept grammarian. The field seized is always deemed to belong to its first owner; this is compared with Roman law. Why hostile devastation of a field falls on the owner and not the robber, and when. Why flooding falls on the owner's risk. What a man suffers in his own field through the robber's fault is to be made good by the robber, Roman law.

units.la: De loco, ubi res aliena domino restituenda. Ann.1. יתיוב. קפ. 2 Ex Gemara explicatur casus, quo rem alienam in desertum deferre liceat. Error S. Iarchi in Gem. expl. Depositum & similia, ubi reddenda, ex jure civ. Rom.
units.tr: On the place where another's property is to be restored to its owner. Note: [יתיוב], [קפ]. The case in which it is lawful to carry another's property into the desert is explained from the Gemara. The error of Rashi in explaining the Gemara. A deposit and similar things, where they are to be returned, from Roman civil law.

units.la: De eo qui dubitat, an alteri suum restituerit: quive dubitat, an alterius rem habuerit. Ann.1 Dubium an alteri suum restituerit, in foro civili nihil debere.2 Regula, כרי ופמ' כרי פרוף. quam Romana leges cum distinctione admittunt. Dubius an debeat, seipsum ignorare, apud Ebr. jurat. De confitente reo in jure Romano.
units.tr: On one who doubts whether he has restored to another what is his own, or who doubts whether he had another's property. Note: it is doubtful whether he restored to another what was his, in the civil forum he owes nothing. The rule [כרי ופמ' כרי פרוף], which Roman laws admit with a distinction. One who is in doubt whether he ought to pay is ignorant of himself, according to the Hebrew oath. On a defendant confessing in Roman law.

units.la: Pecus domino restituta, quæ postea aufertur, vel moritur. Ann.1 Pecudem etiamsi eam restituerit, quare compenset fur denuò surreptam.2 Si dominus pecudem a fure restitutā noverit, de ulteriori damno non teneri furem. Furem quandoque de pecudis vitio teneri, quod analogicè etiam ex legibus Rom. desumitur.
units.tr: Cattle restored to the owner, which afterwards are stolen away or die. Note: even though he restored the beast, why the thief compensates when it is stolen again. If the owner knew that the beast had been restored by the thief, the thief is not liable for further loss. That the thief is sometimes liable for a defect in the beast, which is also derived by analogy from Roman laws. [sic]

units.la: Quæ à quibus emere liceat. Ann. Ratio, quare hædum, lac, lanam à pastoribus emere non liceat. Vbi dominus pastorum factum scire potest, emere ab iis licitum. Quare lintea & pannos à mulieribus emere liceat. Vitulosque in Sarone à pastoribus, etiam mulieribus. Saron regio pascua. Saron duorum locorum nomen, non trium. Lydda & Ioppe, ubi. Saronis transjordanensis situs. Carmelus. Basan. Hermon. v locorum etiam nominibus præfigi. Quæ occultari à venditore jubentur, emere non licet. Misna conciliatio. Aquibusvis gallinas & ova cur emere liceat. Quodcunque judicatur furto ablatum, emere interdicitur: etiam jure Romano. ubi & pretio excidit emptor; atque suscipiens rem furtivam pœnali quoque furti actione conveniri potest.
units.tr: From whom it is lawful to buy what things. Note: the reason why it is not lawful to buy a kid, milk or wool from shepherds. Where the owner can know the shepherds' deed, it is lawful to buy from them. Why it is lawful to buy linen and cloths from women. And calves in Sharon from shepherds, even from women. Sharon is a region of pastures. Sharon is the name of two places, not three. Lydda and Joppa, where. The position of Sharon beyond the Jordan. Carmel. Bashan. Hermon. Names of places are also prefixed with v. What the seller orders to be concealed, it is not lawful to buy. The Mishnah's reconciliation. Why it is lawful to buy hens and eggs from anyone. Whatever is judged to have been taken by theft, it is forbidden to buy; also by Roman law, where the buyer also loses the price, and one who receives a stolen thing can be sued by the penal action for theft.

units.la: Flocculi fullonis & carminatoris. Fullo, sartor, faber, quas minutias retineant, quas reddere debeant. An. Fullo, quis. ejus actiones. Marc. 9. 3. explicatur. Carminator, quis. Paterfamilias, in hujusmodi legibus. Quænam sint ista חומין סלש Misna. Fulloni quando plura cedant. Schidia minora fabri; majora esse locatoris. מקרה. Ex Gemara etiam & Misna, lingua Hebraica cognitionem petendam. Matt. 5. 43. ex Gem. illustratur. Odium ab Ebr. defenditur & jubetur, atque etiam vindicta. Quod ad minutias operariorum, spectandam consuetudinem. Variè hæc de restitutione operariorum cum jure Romano conferuntur. Superstitio Iudaorum.
units.tr: Tufts of the fuller and of the carder. The fuller, tailor, smith: what small remnants they keep and what they must return. Note: the fuller, who he is, his actions. Mark 9:3 is explained. The carder, who he is. The paterfamilias in laws of this kind. What those things are, [חומין סלש], in the Mishnah. When more falls to the fuller. Smaller pieces belong to the smith, larger ones to the employer. [מקרה]. Knowledge of the Hebrew language is to be sought from the Gemara and Mishnah as well. Matt. 5:43 is illustrated from the Gemara. The Hebrews defend hatred and command it, and also vengeance. As to the small remnants of workmen, custom is to be considered. These matters about restitution of workmen are variously compared with Roman law. Superstition of the Jews.
בבא קמא [Bava Kamma]
OR
THE FIRST CODE
Of the forensic laws of the Israelite people:
In Latin
Rendered into Latin, and compared with the laws of others, above all the Romans.
Rendered into Latin, and compared with the laws of others, above all the Romans.
Bava Kamma [בבא קמא]
Chapter 1 [פרק א׳]
Halakhot 1, 1 [הלכי א׳ ו׳]

units.la: ארבע אבות נזיקין השור והבור והמבער והמבער לא הרי השור כהרי הָמבער ולא הרי המבער כהרי השור ולא זה וזה שיש בהם רוח חיים כהרי האש שאין בו רוח חיים ולא זה חד שדרכן לילך ולהזיק כהרי הבור שאין דרכו לילך ולהזיק הצד השור שכהן שדרכן להזיק ושמירתן עליך וכשהזיק חב המזיק לשלם השלומי נזק במיטב הארץ׃
units.tr: The four primary categories of damage: the ox, the pit, the one who kindles fire [המבער]. The ox is not like the one who kindles fire, nor the one who kindles fire like the ox. Nor is it the case that both have a living spirit, as fire has no living spirit. Nor is the one that walks about and harms like the pit, which does not walk about and harm. The ox, whose habit is to harm, is under your watch [שמירתן עליך]. When it harms, the offender must pay full damages from the best of the land [במיטב הארץ].
IN THE YEAR

units.la: ¹ Talmudistæ in constituendo summa capita revocare so- lent, ad quæ subsequentes specia- les casus generatim continea- tur; unde sæpe fe- rantur, ut quid de singulis statuunt.
units.tr: ¹ In setting out their main headings, the Talmudists are accustomed to recall them, under which the following particular cases are generally included. Hence they are often cited for what they lay down about each individual case.
THE FIRST BOOK OF THE CODE
Chapter I.

units.la: Quatuor sunt damnorum fontes: bos; puteus; depascens; incendium. Non ita se habet bos, ut depascens; nec depascens, ut bos; nec hic, & ille, in quibus est vitalis spiritus, ut ignis qui spiritu vitali destituitur; nec denique hic & ille, qui ambulando solent nocere, ut puteus qui non solet ambulando nocere. Conditio aequalis in istis hace est, quod nocere solent, iisque attendere debeas: & quum horum aliquo damnum infertur, ladens teneatur. damni pretium solvere è praestantissimo proventu.
units.tr: There are four sources of damage: the ox, the pit, the grazing animal, and fire. The ox is not in the same position as the grazing animal, nor the grazing animal as the ox. Nor is this one or that one, in which there is a living spirit, like fire, which lacks a living spirit. Nor, finally, are this one and that one, which usually do harm by walking, like the pit, which does not usually do harm by walking. The condition in these is the same in that they are accustomed to do harm, and you must attend to them. When damage is inflicted by any of these, the one causing it is bound to pay the price of the damage out of the best of his produce.
DISPUTATIONS.

units.la: tutionibus suis ea quae tractant ad lent: non quod singula istis capitintur; sed eo saltem hac ratione realis judicandum sit ex istis summis capitibus liqueat. quæ idcirco פנאח, ac si patres dicerent, nuncupant: sicuti ea quæ inde dijudicantur & profluunt, iisdem dicuntur תולדות, generationes. Hinc codice Schabbath f.22. p.1. circa medium, פר רבוח מאבח, pater omnium istorum sanguis est: quia uti glossa explicat, ממנו כולם יצאו, ex eo discuntur omnia, quorum istic mentio. Quod si autem illæ תולדות longius à suis פנאח distent, alia sæpe jura recipiunt: prout ea de re videre est Judæorum judicia in commentariis ad c.2.Haggæi, ‎f.13. Sed nobis de ipsis sermo est, quatenus aliorum ex aliis jura ac conditiones patefiunt. Ut liquet è Maimonide t.4.1.1.c.2.Iad.
units.tr: In their treatises they set out the matters they handle under these headings. This is not because every single case is included under these chief heads, but so that at least by this method it may be clear how judgment is to be made from these principal heads. For this reason they call them by the name [אבות] "fathers," as if they said "fathers," just as the things judged and derived from them are called [תולדות] "generations." Hence in the tractate Shabbath, folio 22, page 1, about the middle: "the father of all these is blood," because, as the gloss explains, "from it all of them come forth" [ממנו כולם יצאו], that is, all the cases mentioned there. But if those generations stand far from their fathers, they often receive other laws, as may be seen from the Jewish judgments in the commentaries on Haggai, chapter 2, folio 13. But we are speaking of them only so far as the laws and conditions of some are made clear from others, as is evident from Maimonides, part 4, book 1, chapter 2, Iad.

units.la: ² Itaque in damnis explicandis quatuor hoc loco פנאח, patres, constituuntur: bos, puteus, depascens, incendium. Non quasi huc damna, de quibus in sequentibus agět author, omninò revocari queant (nam cum per bovem, ejus pedem intelligant Talmudistæ, quid de cornu, quo pauperies facta fuerit, dicendum?) sed ista omnia quæ semper (etsi non ubiq; uti de dente & pede, nocentibus in loco publico, liquet è Gem. f.5. p.1. hujus codicis Babæ Kamæ) perfectè compensari debent: quum bos cornu feriens quandoque (ut si petulcus esse ignoretur) tanta multa non teneatur. Unde in Gemara legitur: de iis quæ ab initio convicta sunt (ideoque totum damnum compensare debent) docet, de innocentibus tandemque convictis non docet. Quæ sint animalia convicta, quæ innocentia, postea liquebit. Quum ergo in Mishna nostra primo loco ponitur bos, pedem intellige omnium interpretum judicio: ubi enim pauperies à jumento facta describitur, id ejus membrum concinnè totius bestiæ nomine notari putant, quod ipsis in nocendo commune est. Et quum damnum pede datum ut fontem constituunt, incessum considerant, si forte quid inter eundum frangat & conculcet. Atq; תולדות, generationes, sive consectaria hic quosdam male statuisse רבות & פועל (refragante cum aliis Maim.c.1.§.10.in Iad. t.4.) docet Gemara. Quorum illo notatur, si quando progressum jumentum rei alicui incumbat eamque confringat; hoc vero, si recalcitrando frangat. Melius alia proponi solent. Veluti si incedens jumentum laedat (inquit Gemara) בסלי onere sibi imposito, frano oris sui & jugo quod collo suo impositum sit. (istud סלא in Aruch exponitur Ephippium, & משוא, onus. posteriori modo accipio: quia pro eo hic alius habet מרדין, quo magnus saccus ad merces deferendas designatur.) Huc referri posset e ff. Si quadrupes.l.1.§.9. Sive autem corpore suo pauperiem quadrupes dedit, sive per aliam rem quam tetigit quadrupes; haec actio, de qua ibidem, locum habebit. ut puta si plaustro bos obtrivit aliquem, vel alia re dejecta. Sic ubi de puteo agunt in Gemara, ad eum referunt ut consectarium, si quis כיור, puteum suum, aut מים, mucum narium in terram dejiciat, quibus lubrica reddatur via ut alius prolabatur: hunc enim casum cum eo conferunt, ubi quis in puteum incidit. Sequitur מבעה, depascens pecus, & a plerisque (ut Gemarae disputationes praetermittam) ad dentem applicatur, quo pecora depasci arva solent. expositionis ratio in Gemara affertur haec, quod Obadiae v. f. 6. hae voces מצפונו in paraphrasi M. Iosephi reddantur מטמוניו, manifestantur absconditae ejus, dentes vero in agro depascendo jam tegantur, jam denudentur. Praefero tamen Maimonidae rationem, מבעה de dente intelligi, quia dente pecora quaerunt & evellunt herbas: magis enim cum vocis proprietate convenit. Ad hanc autem pauperiem quam quadrupes dentibus facit, tanquam consectarium referunt damnum, quod corpore suo dat ubi se scabit, & parieti affricat, qui inde quandoque laeditur; vel arbori eo modo nocet. Tandem quartus fons proponitur, incendium: ubi ignis metam frumenti aliaque absumit. Quo tanquam תולדת revocant damna ab iis data, qui lapides, cultros, onera ac familia ita in summo tecto relinquunt, ut ברוח, vento ordinario, dimoveri inde queant: namque istis in publica loca decidentibus, variis damnis occasionem præbent. Hinc jam patet, quid quatuor illis fontibus damnorum, five οπνη ηιαϸ designetur; & qui ad singulos fontes sive capita, alia multa reducantur, quæ illorum jura sequuntur & conditionem imitantur. (quamvis & hic multæ ratio ac conditio sæpe diversa sit: quatenus jam convicta censentur animalia ad hæc vel illa opera; ad alia non item. quod in præcedentibus exemplis expendendum ex Maim. cod. οπνη c. 1. §. 5. vel quod ννϲ, mutatio, in facto interveniat: ut in quibusdam exemplis c. 2. hujus cod. §. 1.) deinde præter ista damna esse quidem alia; sed quę perfectam compensationem nonnisi certis casibus requirant. 6 Cæterum ne quis excipiat, unicum fontem, vel saltem illorum quosdam sufficere, quò deinde reliqua damna & pauperies (ut loquuntur leges Romanæ) revocentur; pergit in hac Misna D. Judas, & singulos fontes necessarios esse indicat. Inter se differre, ideoque ad unum vel pauciores, quam designaverat, referri non posse docet: quatenus non solum ipsorum natura eadem non est; sed etiam jura in iis observanda differunt. Etenim uti solent Magistri ex una specie colligere aliam; hic una species sufficere videri queat: sed ilico daretur exceptio. Ex. gratia, ... Si scripsisset Misericors illud de dente; dicerem, dentem, quia percipitur commodum ex damno inde dato, obstringere; pedem, quia nulla ex ejus damno utilitas, non obstringere. Cujusmodi plura in hac materia proferri possent. Huc accedit, quod in istis fontibus damnorum non fit eadem juris ratio. Nam, verbi gratia, Deus hic in Gem. f. 5. putei mentionem ita fecisse dicitur ..., ut eo excipiat hominem: quia Exod. 21. 33. legitur, Ceciderit illuc bos, aut asinus. unde concludunt, si homo ceciderit, qui prævidere potuit, alterum illum non teneri. Itaque ob hæc & similia distincte singula proponuntur: cum hic quædam ita excipiantur, quæ alibi non item. Cæterum bovem quum a decadente pascente distinguit, id de pede incedentis bovis, & dente bovis depascentis accipe, (ut è dictis ex parte liquet) nempe pauperiem pede datam, illi quæ dente fit esse dissimilem. Porrò phrasin quod attinet, de מזק dici posset, non esse Chald. ecce, sed quod Talmudici per שור efferunt ex eadem radice: nisi quod מזק fit ex Hiphil. id confirmatur è phrasi seq. ושור; si conferas nostram versionem Halichoth olam, inde à pag.127. Quod ubi feceris, nullum erit de eo dubium. 7 Vbi autem inquit, hiς & ille qui ambulando solent nocere, bovem incedentem ac depascentem intelligit, & ignem qui serpendo & ulteriora consumendo ambulare videtur: quem utrumque distinguit à puteo; utpote qui suo loco immobilis manet. Istam differentiam in Gemara hac phrasi explicant, non est aspectus hujus, sicut aspectus illius: id est, status ac conditio utriusque diversa est. quæ formula in argumentis comparatis est usitatissima: siquidem ibi post varias adversus æqualitatem & similitudinem exceptiones, tandem in ista diversitate, inæqualitate & dissimilitudine convenientiam quandam eruentes subjicere solent, non est conditio hujus, ut illius; status æqualis est, quod, &c. (de quibus consule Clavem Talmudicam, ubi ejusmodi omnia copiosè lectoribus propositui.) 8 Quemadmodum etiam hoc loco, licet nulla sit argumentatio; posterior formula usurpatur, quum dicitur, latus æquale, id est, communis status ac conditio, sive jus æquale quod in quatuor dictis fontibus reperitur. Fortean lectoribus non ingratum erit, si hæc Judaici juris in damnis divisio cum juris Romani divisione conferatur in eadem materia. Hic ejusmodi expressam in quatuor membra divisione mihi non succurrere fateor, attamen singula reperiuntur. & quidem primum ac tertium superioris divisionis membrum in prima differentia ab autore conjunctum, id est, bovem pede denteque lædentem quod attinet; confer ultima verba notæ secundæ, item sententiam istam, ubi Diocletianus & Maximianus ita scribunt, De his quæ per injuriam depasta contendis, ex sententia legis Aquilia agere minimè prohiberis: Cod.li.3. tit.35.le.sin. Et hæc verba, Ex sententia, satis ostendunt, quemadmodum Judæi certa habebant capita, unde de reliquis judicabant; ita Romanis non fuisse omnia legibus certis definita, sed alia ex aliis deducta etiam fuisse. Hoc vero loco totam legem, Si quadrupes pauperiem, è Digest.li.9.tit. 1. non produco: quia lex ista hujusmodi etiam casus continet, qui hac Misna non comprehenduntur. Porrò reliqua duo, puteus, incendium, ab iisdem etiam considerantur, ut damnis occurratur: puteus quidem sive fossa Dig.l.9.tit.2.l.28. Qui foveas, ursorum, cervorumque, capiendorum causa faciunt, si in itineribus secerunt, eoque aliquid decidit, factumque deterius est, lege Aquilia obligati sunt. Item ff. li. 43. leg. Si filius: Praterea si fossam fecerit in silva publica, & bos meus in eam inciderit, agere possum, &c. Denique de incendio in Romanorum legibus agi, nemo ignorare potest qui vel haec verba legerit, ff. Ad legem Aquiliam leg. 27.§.8. Si quis insulam voluerit meam exurere, & ignis ad vicini insulam pervenerit; Aquilia tenebitur etiam vicino. Ad multam quod attinet, ea hic in Misna nostra irrogatur, quæ sacris literis definitur: siquidem Deus Exod.22.5. ita præcipit, Si quis depascens agrum aut vineam immiserit pecus suum quod pascat in agro alterius; optimo agri sui, & optimo vineæ suæ rependito. Nam compensatio ex optimo & præstantissimo in una quidem damni specie præcipitur; sed analogicè hanc ad reliquas enumerat species extendunt. Ideo in genere Abrabaniel ad locum Exodi ... Hinc ajunt S. L. M. Damna æstimant præstantissimo: id est, quum is rependere vult, æstimant rem damnum passam, ac si æquaret dignissimum quod invenitur penes damni authorem. Porrò quia verba legis divinæ, cum dicitur ..., ambigua videntur; ideò uti hic in Gemara f. 6. legimus פלוגי
units.tr: ² Accordingly, in explaining damages, the Hebrew term פנאח is here set out as four fathers (sources): the ox, the pit, the grazing animal, and fire. I do not mean that all the damages the author treats in what follows can be wholly referred back to these heads. (For although the Talmudists understand the ox to mean its foot, what is to be said about the damage done by its horn, by which the harm was done?) Rather, all of these are such that they must always be fully compensated, although not in every case, as is clear from the Gemara, f. 5, p. 1, of this tractate Baba Kamma, concerning a tooth and a foot injuring people in a public place. For when an ox gores with its horn, it sometimes is not liable for such a heavy fine, for instance if its viciousness was unknown. Hence the Gemara reads: "It teaches concerning those animals which were found to be dangerous from the beginning (and therefore must make full compensation for the damage), but it does not teach concerning those that were innocent and only afterwards convicted." Which animals are to be counted dangerous and which innocent will become clear later. Since the ox is put first in our Mishnah, understand the foot, by the judgment of all the commentators. For where the Mishnah describes damage done by a beast of burden with its foot, they think that the limb is neatly named for the whole animal, since harming is common to all of them. And when they set the damage done by the foot as the first source, they consider walking, in case it happens to break and trample something along the way. The Gemara teaches that some have wrongly set down רבות and פועל as the generations or consequences (Maimonides, in the Iad, t. 4, c. 1, §10, disagrees with the others). The first of these refers to the case where a beast in its progress falls upon some thing and breaks it; the second, where it breaks something by kicking. Other examples are usually put forward, and better ones. For instance, if a walking beast injures (says the Gemara) by the load laid upon it, by the bridle of its mouth, and by the yoke placed upon its neck. (The word סלא is explained in the Aruch as saddle, and משוא as burden. I take it in the latter sense, because another text here has מרדין, which designates a large sack for carrying merchandise.) To this could be referred the Digest, Si quadrupes, l. 1, §9: "But whether a quadruped has caused damage by its body, or by some other thing which the quadruped touched, this action, of which the same passage speaks, will apply; for example, if an ox has struck someone with a cart, or has thrown down something else." So too, where they discuss the pit in the Gemara, they refer as a consequence to the case where someone throws his cistern water or the mucus of his nose onto the ground, making the way slippery so that another falls; for they compare this case with that in which someone falls into a pit. Next comes מבעה, the grazing animal, and most apply it (to pass over the Gemara's disputes) to the tooth, with which animals usually graze the fields. The reason for this interpretation is given in the Gemara as follows: in Obadiah v. f. 6, these words מצפונו in the paraphrase of Rabbi Joseph are rendered מטמוניו, its hidden things are revealed, while the teeth, in grazing the field, are sometimes covered and sometimes bared. I prefer, however, Maimonides' explanation that מבעה is to be understood of the tooth, because animals seek and tear out herbs with their teeth; this agrees better with the proper sense of the word. To this damage done by a quadruped with its teeth, they refer as a consequence the damage that it does with its body when it scratches itself and rubs against a wall, which is sometimes injured by this; or it harms a tree in the same way. Finally, the fourth source is put forward, fire, when it consumes a heap of grain and other things. To this, as a generation, they refer the damage done by those who leave stones, knives, loads, or household goods on the top of a roof in such a way that they can be shifted from there by an ordinary wind; for when these fall into public places, they give occasion for various damages.
