units.la: 2 Samuel. mille currus intelligantur. pariter cum idem scriptor dicit septingentos, aliquid reticetur, quod subaudiendum sit. Unde Abrabaniel ad hunc paragraphum annotat, istos septingentos esse פרשים, præfectos equitum qui in castris erant; verum sub istis alios militasse: כל פרשים גדולים וקטנים, ut omnes equites primores & inferiores, sive quicunque in equis equitarent, fuerint septies mille. qui in Chron. memorantur. Si in priori voce sit ellipsis, cur eam in posteriori non admittamus? Quid impedit, quo minus uno loco primarios numeraverit, & quot in universum fuerint in medio reliquerit? Sic solet S. S. hic ellipsin admittere, quam alibi supplet: quo nostram diligentiam acuat. Quemadmodum in arcis Hierosolymitanæ expugnatione 2 Sam.8.idem scriptor eundem loquendi modum adhibens, dixisse Davidem refert, Quisquis percusserit Iebusæum, & ipsos cæcos & claudos; nec addit, quid isti David promiserit: at in Chronicis l.1. c.11. ₵6. Quisquis percusserit Iebusæum primum, futurus est primarius & princeps. Porrò licet S. Jarchi Syriam in Mishna commemoratam, Syriam Tsobæam esse annotaverit (cujus dicti occasione hæc interserenda duxi) in textu tamen Talmudico simpliciter Syriæ sit mentio. Quocirca tanta Synecdoche opus non est, cum Syria, licet in Sacris subinde strictius sumta, apud alios authores latissimæ sit significationis: ut præter hostes istos, qui dictis jam locis recensentur; etiam ulteriores gentes complecti queat. In ista Syria hoc permittit constitutio, ut parvæ pecudes & minuta animalia pascantur: cujus hæc est ratio, quia arbitratur ipsam (Syriam scilicet) proprie non dici (& censeri) subjugatam, atque se habere instar peregrina terra; in terra autem peregrina educare (ista animalia) licere, neque nos habitata (ab Israëlitis) terra in eo metuere. Quorum verborum hic est sensus, in terra Israëlitica istam pastionem esse interdictam, quia ista regio est absolutè Israëlitarum, ideoq; locis istic habitatis consulendum, ne damnum patiantur: at Syriam, licet magna ex parte in Israëlitarum potestatem redacta esset; nihilominus aliis infinitis ad inhabitandum concessam, adeoque non ita subjugatam fuisse, quemadmodum quidem terra Canaan, quæ tota omnino fit Israëlis. unde quæ isthic loca deserta & sylvosa non sunt, eorum respectu habitata terra nuncupantur: cui hac constitutione consultum fuit. Verum hic dubium occurrit de regione Babylonica, quandoquidem eò migrarunt Judæi. Si illud interdictum in Judæorum & Israëlitarum gratiam sancitum sit, omninò Judæi alii aliis ubique istam æquitatem & benevolentiam exhibere debent, ne pecore suo proximum lædant, ubicunque vitam degant. Itaque in Gemara Magister Houna hæc Rabi verba producit, In Babylonia ita nos gessimus, ut in terra Israëlis, quod minores pecudes concernit, ab eo tempore quo Rabus in Babyloniam venit. Is enim, ut quidam existimant, plures secum sua celebritate & authoritate pertraxit: vel ut nonnulli sentiunt, ipse alios illum morem servare docuit, quod quamplurimos ibi habitare Judæos, adeoque firmam & fixam sedem illic habere, videret. Idcirco Maimonides illam consuetudinem cum ipsius ratione, his verbis dextrè expressit, Pridem Babyloniam terra Israëlitica aquarunt, ut iflic parvas pecudes, parvasque feras educare prohiberent: quia multi agri, & vineta iflic illis temporibus erant Israëlitarum. Quam rationem cum expederet author libri in superioribus memorati Chofchen Hammifpat, hanc inde conclusionem elicuit, f. 449, p. 2. Videtur nos hac in parte Babyloniam usq; non trahi (id est, mores nostros eò non transferre:) quia ratio, cur illud in Babylonia interdictum effet, hæc erat, quod ibi multi agri essent Israëlitarum. & quandoquidem jam id non est, ob hanc rationem illud est abrogatum. Sed ad aves accedamus, in quibus gallos gallinaceos Hierosolymis arcent ac prohibent, idque rerum consecratarum causa. Quæ ratio ut solida & sufficiens habeatur, duo nobis in memoriam revocanda sunt: quorum unum contaminandi modum; alterum verò rerum consecratarum usum spectat. Reptilibus aliisque immundis animalibus personas & cibos immundos reddi, prolixè docetur c.11. Levit. ut commate 31. Ista immunda sunt vobis ex omnibus reptilibus: quisquis tetigerit illa post mortem illorum, immundus erit usque ad vesperam? 32. Et res omnis super quam aliquod eorum post mortem suam ceciderit immunda erit &c. Doctores autem subsumunt, [?] ודך קרנגולין לא[?] Atqui galli gallinacei in ferquilinio scalpere solent: itaque forte ad quantitatem grani lentis de reptili (illuc abjecto) emergeret, & hac ratione contaminabuntur consecrata. Quocirca cum à reptilium tactu res contaminentur, reptilia vero eorumve minimas particulas gallinacei sæpe è sterquilinio, vel aliunde ex terra unguibus fodiendo eruant; magistris placet, gallinaceos arceri, ne si reptilium particulæ scalpendo ejectæ in res consecratas decidant, sancta impurentur. Quod sterquilinii hic mentionem injiciant Judæi, stricte accipiendum non est; sed hoc exemplum ab ipsis adhibetur, quia galli gallinacei in sterquiliniis ut plurimum unguibus fodere solent. Alioqui nulla Hierosolymis deprehendebantur sterquilinia: si Gemaræ fidem habeamus Cod. Baba Kam. edit. Ven. f. 82. p. 2. ubi decem privilegia ordine recensentur, quæ ut curioso lectori inserviam subjicere ac vertere, vel etiam illustrare non gravabor. Ita habet Gemara, [?] ... Decem res dicuntur de Ierusalem. Domus in ipsa non venditur lege mancipii, qua de re Levit. 25. 29. Quum quis vendet domum habitabilem in civitate muro cincta, tum erit jus redemtura ejus usque ad complementum anni venditionis ejus: anno pleno esto jus redemtura ejus. 30. Quod si non fuerit redempta interea dum completur ei annus integer; tunc cedet domus illa quæ est in civitate muro cincta, in mancipium illi qui emit eam per generationes illius. Hæc ultima verba in Gemara arripiunt, quæ Jerosolymæ non competere posse arbitrantur: utpote quam certæ tribui assignatam negant; ad aliquam autem perpetuæ ædium possessione derivari posse, constat. Secundum privilegium ita habet, [?] ... non affert vitulam decollandam.
units.tr: 2 Samuel: the thousand chariots are to be understood. Likewise, when the same writer says seven hundred, something is left unstated that must be supplied. Hence Abrabanel, annotating this paragraph, says that these seven hundred were the פרשים [parashim], commanders of the horsemen who were in the camp; but other men also served under them: כל פרשים גדולים וקטנים [kol parashim gedolim veketanim], so that all the horsemen, chief and lesser, or whoever rode on horses, numbered seven thousand, as recorded in Chronicles. If there is an ellipsis in the first figure, why should we not admit one in the second? What prevents him from counting the chief men in one place and leaving the total in the middle? Sacred Scripture often admits an ellipsis of this kind here, which it supplies elsewhere, so as to sharpen our diligence. So too in the storming of the citadel of Jerusalem, 2 Sam. 8, the same writer, using the same manner of speaking, reports David as saying: Whoever strikes the Jebusite, and the blind and the lame as well; he does not add what David promised to such a man. But in Chronicles, 1 Chr. 11.6, we read: Whoever strikes the Jebusite first shall be chief and prince. Moreover, although S. Jarchi, annotating the Mishnah, has noted that the Syria mentioned there is Syria Zobah (and since this remark prompts it, I thought this should be inserted here), the Talmudic text simply speaks of Syria. Hence there is no need for so great a synecdoche, since Syria, though sometimes taken more narrowly in the Sacred books, has a very wide meaning in other authors, so that it can embrace, besides those enemies already listed in the passages cited, also more distant peoples. In this Syria the law permits small cattle and small animals to be pastured. The reason for this is that it is thought that it (Syria, namely) is not properly called, or considered, subjugated, and that it stands as a foreign land; and that in a foreign land it is lawful to rear (these animals), nor do we fear for an inhabited land (of the Israelites) in this respect. The sense of these words is this: pasturing of this kind is forbidden in the land of Israel, because that region belongs absolutely to the Israelites, and therefore the places inhabited there must be consulted, lest they suffer loss; but Syria, although for the most part reduced to Israelite power, was nevertheless granted to countless others to dwell in, and so was not subjugated in the way the land of Canaan certainly was, which wholly belongs to Israel. Hence, the places there that are not desert or wooded are called inhabited land in relation to them, and this is the provision that was made by this law. Yet here a doubt arises about the Babylonian region, since the Jews migrated there. If that prohibition was enacted for the sake of the Jews and Israelites, then all Jews, wherever they live, must show this same fairness and goodwill to one another, so as not to harm their neighbour with their flocks. Accordingly, in the Gemara, Master Huna brings forward these words of Rabbi: In Babylonia we have behaved as in the land of Israel, as far as lesser cattle are concerned, from the time when Rabbi came to Babylonia. For he, as some think, drew many with him by his fame and authority; or, as some judge, he himself taught others to keep that custom, since he saw that very many Jews lived there and so had a firm and fixed seat there. Hence Maimonides expressed that custom together with its reason skilfully in these words: Long ago they forbade Babylon, which is not the land of Israel, to rear small cattle and small beasts there, because at that time many fields and vineyards there belonged to the Israelites. When the author of the book Choshen Hammishpat, mentioned above, set out this reasoning, he drew from it this conclusion, f. 449, p. 2: It seems that in this respect we are not carrying our customs over to Babylon (that is, we do not transfer our practices there), because the reason why that was forbidden in Babylon was that there were many fields there belonging to the Israelites; and since this is no longer so, that prohibition has been repealed on this ground. But let us come to birds, among which the rabbis keep and forbid domestic cocks in Jerusalem, and this for the sake of holy things. For this reason to be regarded as sound and sufficient, two points must be recalled to us: one concerns the manner of contamination, the other the use of holy things. That persons and food are made unclean by reptiles and other unclean animals is taught at length in Lev. 11, as in verses 31 and 32: These are unclean to you among all reptiles; whoever touches them after their death shall be unclean until evening. And every thing on which any of them falls after its death shall be unclean, etc. The teachers, moreover, argue: [?] ... But cocks are wont to scratch in a dunghill; so perhaps some particle of a reptile (thrown there) might come up, about the size of a lentil grain, and by this means the holy things would be contaminated. Hence, since things are contaminated by touching a reptile, and cocks often dig out with their claws very small particles of reptiles from a dunghill or elsewhere in the earth, the masters have decided that cocks should be kept away, lest, if particles of reptiles flung out by scratching should fall upon holy things, the sacred things be defiled. That the Jews here mention a dunghill is not to be taken strictly; this example is adduced by them simply because cocks usually dig with their claws in dunghills. Otherwise no dunghills were found in Jerusalem, if we trust the Gemara, Cod. Baba Kamma, Venice ed., f. 82, p. 2, where ten privileges are listed in order. I will not hesitate to set these down for the curious reader, to translate them and even to illustrate them. The Gemara reads: [?] ... Ten things are said of Jerusalem. A house in it is not sold by the law of purchase, concerning which Lev. 25.29: When a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, he shall have the right of redemption within a full year of its sale; for a full year shall be his right of redemption. 30: But if it is not redeemed within the space of a full year, then the house that is in the walled city shall pass in perpetuity to him who bought it, throughout his generations. The Gemara seizes on these last words, which they think cannot apply to Jerusalem, since it is denied that it was assigned to a particular tribe; yet it is agreed that it can be derived to the perpetual possession of some buildings. The second privilege reads: [?] ... it does not bring forth a heifer to be beheaded.

units.la: Cujus cognitio è cap. 21. Deut. dependet: ubi ad cædem in agro factam expiandam, si ignoretur author, proximæ civitatis seniores vitulam in vallem deducere jubentur, ibique super vitulam manus lavare tenentur. Quia istius legis initio dicitur, Si inveniatur confossus, in terra quam Iova Deus tuus dat tibi ut hereditario jure possideas eam; ideo Jerusalem illa obligatione vitulam adducendi eximunt, quod tribus certæ cum aliis regionibus distributa non sit. Tertium his verbis efferunt, non fit civitas impulsa: quasi dicerent, non subjicitur legibus Deut. 13.12. & seq. quibus graves pœnæ in eam civitatem decernuntur, quæ ad idololatriam quorundam suasu impulsa fuit. Etenim quia ꝡf.12. civitatum tuarum legimus; ideo ad rationem in primo & secundo privilegio adductam respicientes, urbem istis etiam pœnis eximunt. Quartum est, quod non contaminetur plagis lepra: quia tribubus in possessionem distributa non fuit; lepra vero in ædibus regionis possessionis ipsorum erat Lev.14.34. Quinta proprietas, quod in ea non promittant sive è parietibus educant trabes, nec podia sive pergulas pendulas. Ratio duplex, prior ex tentorio immunditiæ desumitur: quo loquendi modo ad comma 14. Num. 19. c. respiciunt. Quum homo mortuus fuerit in tentorio; quisquis accedit ad tentorium ipsum, & quisquis est in ipso tentorio, immundus esto septem dies. Iam fieri posse, inquiunt, ut minima cadaveris particula in terra occultetur; podia autem ista sive superiores pergulas veluti tentoria esse supra subjectum spacium: ideoque omnes prætereuntes infra podia contaminari ex illa de tentorio lege. Altera ratio, ne si quid è superiori loco decidat, eorum qui festa frequentant nonnulli lædantur. Sextò addunt, In ipsa non accumulant sterquilinia. Atque hoc est cujus occasione hæc producimus: id enim probandum erat, in Jerusalem ex illo privilegio non fuisse sterquilinium. Septimò addunt,
units.tr: The knowledge of this depends on Deut. 21. There, to expiate a killing done in the field, if the author is unknown, the elders of the nearest city are ordered to lead a heifer down into a valley and are bound to wash their hands over the heifer. Because at the beginning of that law it is said: If one is found slain in the land which the LORD your God gives you to possess by inheritance, therefore they exempt Jerusalem from the obligation of bringing the heifer, because it was not distributed to a particular tribe along with other regions. They express the third in these words: a city is not led astray, as if they meant: it is not subject to the laws of Deut. 13.12 and following, by which severe penalties are decreed against a city that has been led into idolatry by the persuasion of certain men. For since we read of your cities in verse 12, therefore, looking to the reason adduced in the first and second privileges, they exempt the city from these penalties as well. The fourth is that it is not defiled by plagues of leprosy, because it was not distributed to the tribes as a possession; but leprosy occurs in the houses of the land of their possession, Lev. 14.34. The fifth property is that they do not extend (that is, do not lead out from the walls) beams, nor balconies or hanging galleries. The reason is twofold: the first is drawn from the tent of uncleanness, to which they refer in the words of Num. 19.14: When a man dies in a tent, whoever enters the tent, and whoever is in the tent, shall be unclean seven days. They argue that it can happen that the smallest particle of a corpse is hidden in the ground; and these balconies, or upper galleries, are like tents over the space beneath, so that all who pass beneath the balconies would be contaminated by that law of the tent. The other reason is that if anything should fall from a higher place, some of those who attend the festivals might be hurt. Sixth, they add: In it they do not heap up dunghills. And this is the matter on account of which we bring these things forward: for this had to be proved, that in Jerusalem, by that privilege, there was no dunghill. Seventh, they add,

units.la: { } Hebrew and Greek phrases appear in the text and are not reproduced here. Non struunt in eo fornaces; ne fumus civitatem pervadat: ut ipsi annotant. Id de fornacibus calcariis intellige: quemadmodum S. J. Gen. 19. 28. Fornax calcaria est locus excavatus, ubi saxa comburunt in calcem. Octavo, In ea non plantant hortos, aut pomaria, praeter rosceta quae jam inde a priorum prophetarum temporibus ibi fuere. Nam ista loca stercorare solent; at sterquilinia hic prohibentur. deinde inquiunt propter spurcitiem qua voce non tantum peccatum; sed etiam, quod hujus loci est, Zizaniam malignasque herbas denotant. Nono, In ea gallinaceos non alunt: qua de re satis in superioribus. Decimum quod ibi fieri negant, ita exprimunt, mortuum ibi pernoctare non permittunt. Itaque si ibi moriatur homo, eo ipso die statim illum sepeliunt. Huic postremo subjiciunt, traditio: quasi dicas, nulla quidem sufficiens ratio apparet; sed hoc ἀπὸ ὑπομνήματος a majoribus acceptum fuit. Tamen ibi sunt sepulchra familiae Davidicae & Huldae Prophetissae; ut observatur in Additione (Hipsim vocant) ad c. 1. Babae postremae. Supra, initio hujus tertiae notae duo expendenda dicebantur, quo perciperetur, qua ratione res consecratae gallinaceos urbe sancta expellebant: itaque jam ad secundum accedamus, puta rerum consecratarum usum. Res sanctae (uti e Maimonide Cod. Maase Hakkorbanoth c. 1. sect. 4. cum 17. & c. 10. 7. colligitur manifeste) ex animalis desumtae in duas classes dividuntur: quarum posterior res sanctissimas continet, ut sunt holocausta, victimae pro peccato & reatu, nec non eucharistica coetus totius; reliqua eucharistica, sacrificia laudis, aliaque ut primogenita, decimae & paschalis agnus, priorem classem constituunt, ac sancta levia dicuntur. Quae posteriora ubi comederentur, in urbe sancta iis vesci Israelitae jubebantur, secundum Talmudicum pronunciatum Cod. Celim, cap. 1. quo Jerusalem reliquis civitatibus sanctior censetur, quia ipsi comedunt sancta levia & decimas secundas. Atque haec sacris literis convenienter dicuntur: nam de sanctis quibusdam levioribus, uti vocant, legimus Deut. 15. 19. Coram Iova Deo tuo comedito illud (primogenitum) quotannis in loco quem elegerit Iova; tu & familia tua. De decimis secundis Deut. 14. 26. Expensa pecunia illa (ex decimis secundis in loco nimis remoto redacta) in omnia quae desideraverit animus tuus in boves, aut in pecudes, & in vinum, aut in alium potum inebriantem, denique in omnia quae expetierit abs te animus tuus; comedes ibi coram Iova Deo tuo. Hisce Judaei suam traditionem confirmant. De sanctis vero sanctissimis intra civitatem edi solitis, consulendum caput quintum de Sacrificiis. Audivimus sancta inquinari posse gallinaceis, qui reptilium particulas e terra scalpendo eruunt; deinde sancta quamplurima in sancta civitate comedi: quapropter, ne sancta a gallinaceis inquinentur, hi in urbem ita non admittuntur, ut ibi alantur. At sacerdotibus gallinaceos alicubi in terra Canaan habere non licebat. Hoc enim puritates impediebant. Qui, quave ratione? Responsio e sacerdotum & primitiarum (ut hanc vocem latius cum V. L. usurpem,) statu ac conditione dependet. Isti, quae sibi primitiae consecrabantur, iis ipsis per totam regionem Canaan vescebantur; atqui, ut Maimonides observat Cod. de primitiis c. 12. sect.
units.tr: Hebrew and Greek phrases appear in the text and are not reproduced here. They do not build furnaces in it, lest the smoke spread over the city, as they themselves note. Understand this of lime-kilns, as in Gen. 19. 28: A lime-kiln is a hollowed-out place where stones are burned into lime. Eighth, In it they do not plant gardens or orchards, except the rose beds which have been there since the time of the earlier prophets. For such places are usually manured, whereas dunghills are forbidden here. Then they say on account of the filth, a word which denotes not only sin but also, as is relevant here, darnel and noxious weeds. Ninth, In it they do not keep fowls, about which enough was said above. The tenth thing they say is not done there, they express thus: they do not allow a dead body to remain overnight there. So if a man dies there, they bury him that same day. To this last point they add tradition, as if to say that no sufficient reason appears, but that this was received from the elders as a memorial [ἀπὸ ὑπομνήματος]. Nevertheless, there are the tombs of the Davidic family and of the prophetess Huldah, as is observed in the Addition (called Hipsim) to chapter 1 of Baba postrema. Above, at the beginning of this third note, two things were said to need consideration, so that it might be understood by what reason consecrated things drove fowls out of the holy city. So let us now come to the second, namely the use of consecrated things. Holy things (as is clearly gathered from Maimonides, Code Maase Hakkorbanoth, ch. 1 sect. 4 with 17, and ch. 10 sect. 7) are divided from animals into two classes. The latter contains the most holy things, such as burnt offerings, sacrifices for sin and for guilt, and also the peace offerings of the whole congregation. The rest, namely the peace offerings, sacrifices of praise, and others such as firstborn animals, tithes and the paschal lamb, constitute the former class and are called light holy things. Where these latter were to be eaten, the Israelites were commanded to eat them in the holy city, according to the Talmudic pronouncement in the Code Celim, ch. 1, by which Jerusalem is judged holier than the other cities, because they eat light holy things and second tithes. These things are said in agreement with Holy Scripture, for concerning certain lighter holy things, as they are called, we read in Deut. 15. 19: Before Jehovah your God you shall eat it (the firstborn) every year in the place which Jehovah shall choose; you and your household. Concerning second tithes, Deut. 14. 26: Spend that money (from the second tithes, realized in a place too remote) on whatever your soul desires, on oxen or on sheep, on wine or on other intoxicating drink, in short on anything your soul asks of you; and you shall eat there before Jehovah your God. The Jews confirm their tradition by these texts. Concerning the most holy things, which were customarily eaten within the city, one should consult the fifth chapter, On Sacrifices. We have heard that holy things can be defiled by fowls, which scratch up particles of reptiles from the earth; and that very many holy things were eaten in the holy city. Therefore, lest the holy things be defiled by fowls, these are not admitted into the city so as to be reared there. But priests were not permitted to keep fowls anywhere in the land of Canaan, for this would hinder their purity. Why and in what way? The answer depends on the status and condition of the priests and of the firstfruits (I use this word more broadly with V. L.). Those firstfruits which were consecrated to the priests were eaten by them throughout the whole region of Canaan. But, as Maimonides observes in the Code on Firstfruits, ch. 12, sect.

units.la: 1. Vetitum est hanc oblationem regionis Israelitica contaminare, ut & reliquas sanctitates; nec eam quis deducat in immunditiei periculum. Hac de causa gallinaceos non alebant sacerdotes; ne immunda reptilia eorumve particulae unguibus effossae in sanctas primitias inciderent, eaque contaminarent. Istae vero oblationes per totam terram Canaan a sacerdotibus edebantur: unde & omnibus istis locis galli gallinacei ab aedibus sacerdotum removebantur. 5 At Israelitis ubique interdictum, ne porcos alerent. Causam interdicti in Gemara reddunt: quæ ut eo melius percipiatur, ex Josephi libro 13. & 14. repetendum, post patris obitum inter Hyrcanum & Aristobulum de regno contentionem exortam fuisse. Itaque l. 14. Antiq. c. 1. in hunc modum scribit author, cum Aristobuli victoriam in pugna quadam narrasset: Φεύγει εἰς τὴν ἀκρόπολιν Ὑρκανός, ἔνθα συνέβαινε καὶ ἁρπάζειν τὴν Ἀριστοβούλης γυναῖκα, fugit in arcem Hyrcanus, ubi contigerat concludi Aristobuli uxorem: quam arcem Hierosolymis fuisse c. ult. l. 13. edocet. Hinc liquet Hyrcanum intra urbem, Aristobulum extra eam fuisse, sub ultima saltem istius difficilii tempora. Quocirca narrant Gemarici Doctores, [hebrew text] Quum Hasmonaei alii alios impugnarent, Hyrcanus intra civitatem, Aristobulus extra ipsam erat. quotidie catenis in capsa aliis denarios demittebant; qui ipsis vicissim sursum attollebant jugis sacrificii victimas. Sed cum illic esset senex quidam Gracanica sapientia peritus, dicebat obsidentibus, Quandiu in cultu suo occupantur, in manum vestram non traduntur: eras catenâ demittent denarios in capsa; tum remittite ipsis porcum. qui cum ad muri medium sublatus fuisset, ungulas suas in murum fixit: unde quum commota fuisset terra Israelitica ad quadringentas parasangas quaquaversum, ista hora pronunciarunt, Maledictus vir qui educaverit porcos, & maledictus homo qui filium suum Gracorum sapientiam docuerit. Et quia in promptu erat exceptio, non quidem edendi causa id licere; sed cum eorum arvina & adipe multa linantur ac inungantur, in hunc finem fortasse si collimetur, porcos non prohiberi; ideo & hoc scopo porcum alere interdixerunt. Ita D. Afcher magnæ inter Judæos authoritatis, annotat ad Mifnæ verba, Nullo loco Israëlita porcos educabit, ולפילו כדי למטוח מהן עורות, nequidem ut ungantur iis pelles. Imo addit, nec etiam porcos pascendos ut deinde aliis vendantur, quibus interdicti non sunt. Nec id Judæos excufare, fi ad exercendam mercaturam porcos alicubi alant. Huic Afcheri favet Mifna Cod. Schebiit: ubi cap. fept. fectione 3. legimus, vel fecundum divisionem Jerofolym. 6. אין עושין סחורה לא בכלילות ולא בסריפות ולא בסקקיס ולא כרמטים, Non exercent mercaturam nec morticinis, nec discerptis, nec abominandis, nec reptilibus. Bestias hic prohibent, quarum esu Israëlitis interdictum erat: quarum ambitu sues ac porcos comprehendi, nos docet c. 11. Levit. Vbi quidem istas bestias vendere non prohibetur: sed Gemara Jerofolymitana sub finem c. 7. Babæ primæ, id ex ipsis ca. istius verbis eruere conatur, quum inquit, כתיב ממחיים הם לכם מה תלמוד לומר וממחיים יהיו לכם לא לוכלה ולא לתקרוס ארבע בקבר ולדא מחור לא לאכור Scriptum est (aliquoties c.11.Levit.) Immundi sunt vobis. Quam ergo doctrinam suppeditat (¥f.35.) Et immundi funto vobis? Sed hoc docetur, convenire interdictum de esu, & interdictum de emolumento (id est, quod edere non licet, nec inde aliud emolumentum, ut pretium in vendendo, percipere licet.) Verum in eo quodcunq; illorum (magistrorum) dictis interdicitur, mercaturam exercere licet. Si rei alicujus esus Lege interdicatur, ejusdem mercaturam interdictam volunt: ideoque nec porcorum mercimonium admittunt, utpote qui illo genere continentur. Hic notanda objectio, quam Doctor Simeon annotationibus ad c. 7. Schebiit nobis proponit. וכרי תמור למלוכתו סוא גדל ולמלכתו סוא גדל ולא סקרין לסגות כין סחורה לא Atqui ecce, asinus ad opus suum educatur, ecce etiam camelus ad opus suum educatur; neque prohibent, quominus iis mercatura exerceatur. verum respondeo, Illa de re, qua tantum apta est esui, agitur. Quasi dicat, non alias bestias hic spectaspectamus, quam istiusmodi, quarum alius non est quam in edendo usus; non vero ad laborem subeundum similiave opera adhibentur. Sues vero & porci alium usum, quam ut cibum suppeditent, non habent. Vnde ergo porci, quorum mentio Matt. 8. 30? Nam pascere ipsos, magistrorum saltem authoritas vetabat. Si quis regerat Judæos cum Benjamitis tantum rediisse, unà cum Levitis, reliquas vero tribus in captivitate mansisse; ideo quicquid extra Judæam & Benjaminitidem esset, ab aliis gentibus occupatum, quibus sues prohibitæ non erant: hac ratione iis non satisfaciet, qui totam hanc rem expendent accuratius. Id enim probare non possum, ut loca ista reliqua à gentilibus tantum habitata fuisse asseratur: idque primò ex eo refelli posse antumo, quod Servator noster Mat. 15. 24. testetur, Non sum missus nisi ad oves perditas domus Israëlis, nempe ad annunciandum ore meo euangelium, edendaq; jam miracula; cum tamen passim extra Benjaminis & Judæ tribum prædicaverit euangelium, idque miraculis confirmaverit. quocirca illic passim Israëlitas sedes suas habuisse necesse fuit. Atque hoc indubium meo judicio, cum ob rationem prædictam; tum etiam quia discipulis suis injunxit Christus, ne in viam Gentium abirent, Matt. 10. 5. qui tamen Luc. 9. 6. singulos vicos obibant: puta ubi Christus ambulare solitus erat; uti liquet, si quis Luc. 10. 1. conferat, ubi alios discipulos misisse narratur in omnem urbem & locum, quò futurum erat ut ipse veniret. Concludere merito mihi videor, Israëlitas ibi vixisse: qui non sine causa duplices saltem constitui possent, reduces e captivitate Babylonica; & deinde nonnulli eorum posteri qui à Salmanassare abducti fuerant.
